value.rationale: The TECTON T 5 WH support rail and TECTON SF WH feed-in module are components of a track lighting system designed to provide continuous electrical connection along their length. They are classified under heading 8536 as electrical apparatus for making connections to or in electrical circuits, specifically under subheading 8536.90 as other electrical apparatus, because they function as prefabricated busbar trunking/connectors rather than simple insulated wire or cable of heading 8544.

The TECTON support rail and feed-in module are components of a track lighting system designed to provide mechanical support and electrical connection capabilities. Because they serve as a passive electrical connection system for a voltage not exceeding 1000 V, they are classified under heading 8536 as electrical apparatus for making connections to or in electrical circuits, specifically under subheading 8536.90.

The product is a stuffed textile Halloween decoration depicting the character Zero and a jack-o'-lantern, designed and sold exclusively for the Halloween holiday. It is classified under heading 9505 as a festive article, and specifically under subheading 9505.90 because it is a festive article for a holiday other than Christmas.

The product is a stuffed textile Halloween decoration depicting the character Zero and a jack-o'-lantern, designed and sold exclusively for the Halloween holiday. It is classified under heading 9505 as a festive article, and specifically under subheading 9505.90 because it is a festive article for a holiday other than Christmas.

The product is a stuffed textile Halloween decoration depicting the character Zero from The Nightmare Before Christmas attached to a jack-o'-lantern. In accordance with US Customs ruling NY N314545, this item is classified under heading 9505 as a festive article, specifically subheading 9505.90. Although this correct subheading was omitted from the candidate list, it is the legally correct classification.

The Integrated Performance Computer Unit (IPCU) is an automatic data processing (ADP) machine that meets the requirements of Note 5(A) to Chapter 84, as it processes sensor data and runs artificial intelligence algorithms to facilitate autonomous driving. Because its primary function is data processing rather than performing a specific non-ADP function, it is classified under heading 8471, specifically as a processing unit under subheading 8471.50.

The Integrated Performance Computer Unit (IPCU) is a high-performance computer that processes sensor data and runs AI algorithms to facilitate autonomous driving. It meets the definition of an automatic data processing (ADP) unit under Note 5(C) to Chapter 84. By application of Section XVII Note 2(e), ADP machines of heading 8471 are excluded from Chapter 87, making subheading 8471.50 the correct classification over vehicle parts of heading 8708.

The product consists of decorative garden statues made of iron, which is a base metal. Heading 8306 covers statuettes and other ornaments of base metal, and subheading 830629 specifically covers those not plated with precious metal, aligning with established customs precedents for similar decorative metal items.

Decorative garden statues made of iron are classified under heading 7326 as other articles of iron or steel, as they are not more specifically covered by any other heading in Chapter 73. Subheading 7326.90 is appropriate as these decorative items do not fall under any of the specific subheadings for forged, stamped, or wire articles.

The Neural DSP Quad Cortex is a digital guitar and instrument effects processor that modifies audio signals. It is an electrical apparatus with an individual function not specified or included elsewhere in Chapter 85, which aligns with the established precedent classifying guitar effects processors under subheading 8543.70.

The Neural DSP Quad Cortex is a digital effects processor designed to modify the audio signals of electric guitars and other electrical musical instruments. Since it is an accessory used solely or principally with the electrical musical instruments of heading 9207, it is classified under heading 9209, specifically subheading 9209.94 as an accessory for such instruments.

The product is a life-sized stationary metal cockpit shell designed to be assembled and fitted with equipment to function as an F-16 flight simulator. Flight simulators are classified as ground flying trainers under heading 8805, and because this shell is specifically designed for an F-16 fighter jet simulator, it is classified as a part of an air combat simulator under subheading 8805.21.

The product is a life-sized stationary metal cockpit shell designed to simulate an F-16 fighter jet. Heading 8805 covers ground flying trainers and parts thereof, and subheading 8805.21 specifically covers air combat simulators and parts thereof, which directly encompasses parts of an F-16 fighter jet simulator.

The SD-D05 (A·TRACS) is a composite electronic sensor tag designed to measure, log, and monitor multiple environmental and physical parameters (temperature, humidity, light, and acceleration/shock/tilt). Because it performs multiple measuring and checking functions that are not individually covered by a single more specific heading in Chapter 90 (such as 9025 for temperature or 9027 for light), it is classified under heading 9031 as an instrument or appliance for measuring or checking, not elsewhere specified or included. Specifically, it falls under subheading 9031.80.

The product is an environmental monitoring and condition-sensing tag containing micro-sensors to measure temperature, humidity, light, and acceleration. Among the provided candidate subheadings, heading 8541 covers semiconductor-based transducers under subheading 8541.51, which represents the essential sensing character of the device.

The items are current-carrying electrical support rails functioning as insulated electric conductors with copper conductors extending their entire length. Heading 8544 covers insulated electric conductors, and subheading 854449 properly encompasses those for a voltage not exceeding 1000 volts, not fitted with connectors.

The product is a current-carrying electrical support rail (trunk) equipped with copper conductors that extend along its length to provide a continuous electrical connection for a lighting system. Heading 8544 covers insulated electric conductors, and because these items feature multiple insulated copper conductors designed for a voltage not exceeding 1000 volts and are not fitted with connectors, they are classified under subheading 854449.

The product is a stuffed textile Halloween decoration depicting the character Zero with a jack-o'-lantern. Based on its exclusive use and design as a festive decoration, it is classified under heading 9505 as a festive article. Precedents confirm that similar Halloween novelties and decorations fall under subheading 950590.

The product is a textile Halloween decoration made of stuffed man-made materials. None of the provided candidate subheadings from Chapters 2, 54, 57, 62, or 85 correctly describe textile articles or festive decorations of Chapter 63, but 630790 is the standard provision for made-up textile articles like stuffed decorations.

The product is an Integrated Performance Computer Unit (IPCU) functioning as a centralized control and processing platform for autonomous driving within a vehicle. As an electrical machine with an individual function not specified elsewhere in Chapter 85, it is classified under heading 8543 and specifically subheading 854370. This is consistent with precedents for electronic control modules.

The product is an Integrated Performance Computer Unit (IPCU) functioning as an autonomous driving module designed specifically for motor vehicles. As parts and accessories of motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705 that are not more specifically provided for elsewhere, they fall under heading 8708. Specifically, subheading 870899 covers other parts and accessories of motor vehicles not elsewhere specified.

The product is an iron decorative garden statue, which is classified as an ornamental item of base metal. Heading 8306 specifically provides for statuettes and other ornaments of base metal, and subheading 830629 covers those made of base metal other than plated with precious metal.

The product is an iron decorative garden statue, which is an article of iron or steel not more specifically described elsewhere in the nomenclature. It falls under heading 7326 covering other articles of iron or steel, specifically under subheading 732690 for miscellaneous iron or steel articles.

The product is a digital guitar and instrument effects processor that modifies audio signals electrically. Based on similar customs precedents, electrical sound and effect processors are classified under heading 8543 as electrical machines having individual functions, not specified elsewhere. Therefore, subheading 854370 is the most appropriate classification.

The Neural DSP Quad Cortex is a digital effects processor specifically designed for guitars and other musical instruments. Under Chapter 92 Note 2, parts and accessories suitable for use solely or principally with instruments of heading 9207 are classified in heading 9209. Therefore, as an accessory designed specifically for electric guitars and musical instruments, it falls under subheading 920994.

The product is an F-16 simulator cockpit shell, which is designed to simulate the experience of piloting a fighter jet. Heading 8805 specifically provides for ground flying trainers and air combat simulators and parts thereof, making subheading 880521 the most accurate and specific classification.

The product is an F-16 simulator cockpit shell used to simulate piloting a fighter jet. Heading 8805 specifically provides for ground flying trainers and air combat simulators and parts thereof, making subheading 880521 the correct classification for air combat simulators.

The product is an environmental-monitoring and condition-sensing tag used to measure parameters such as temperature, humidity, light, and shock during transit. Heading 9031 covers measuring or checking instruments, appliances, and machines not specified elsewhere in Chapter 90. Subheading 903180 is the appropriate provision for these kinds of data acquisition and condition-sensing devices.

The product is a composite, self-contained electronic sensor tag equipped with integrated semiconductor-based micro-sensors to measure environmental conditions like temperature, humidity, and acceleration. Heading 8541 covers semiconductor-based transducers, and subheading 854151 specifically provides for semiconductor-based transducers used for sensing physical or environmental phenomena.

The product is a contemporary artwork consisting of a three-dimensional epoxy plastic resin relief mounted in a wooden frame. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of the artwork is imparted by the molded and shaped plastic resin relief component. Consequently, it is classified under heading 3926 as an ornamental article of plastics.

The product is a three-dimensional contemporary artwork made primarily of epoxy resin relief mounted on a panel and framed in wood. As it is an article of plastic not more specifically provided for elsewhere in the nomenclature, it falls under Chapter 39 as other articles of plastics. Heading 3926 covers other articles of plastics, and subheading 392690 applies to miscellaneous plastic articles.

The Hydrapro thermal expansion tank is a welded steel shell container of a capacity not exceeding 300 liters (2 and 4.5 gallons) used to absorb thermally expanded water in a plumbing system. It is properly classified under heading 7310 as a tank of iron or steel with a capacity under 300l, rather than a compressed gas container or a filtering/pumping machine.

The products are diaphragm expansion tanks constructed of welded steel with capacities under 300 liters (2 and 4.5 gallons). They function as steel containers for holding liquid and absorbing pressure fluctuations in a plumbing system. Therefore, they are classified under heading 7310 as iron or steel tanks of a capacity not exceeding 300 liters.

The product is an empty 2.5-gallon plastic jug made of high-density polyethylene, intended for the conveyance or packing of liquid carwash chemicals and not designed for repeated use. Under heading 3923, plastic articles for the conveyance or packing of goods, specifically carboys, bottles, flasks, and similar articles are classified in subheading 392330.

The product consists of empty 2.5-gallon plastic jugs made of high density polyethylene, imported with plastic caps for packing liquid carwash chemicals. Under Heading 3923, plastic articles for the conveyance or packing of goods, specifically carboys, bottles, flasks, and similar articles, are classified in subheading 392330.

The products are vulcanized rubber livestock feeding nipples designed for agricultural animal feeding. As articles of vulcanised rubber not elsewhere specified or included, they fall under heading 4016. Specifically, heading 4014 covers hygienic or pharmaceutical articles including teats, but those are generally understood to be for human use (such as baby bottle nipples); livestock feeding nipples are classified as general non-cellular rubber articles under subheading 401699.

The product consists of vulcanized rubber livestock feeding nipples designed for feeding animals. Heading 4014 specifically covers hygienic or pharmaceutical articles, including teats, of vulcanised rubber other than hard rubber. Subheading 401490 appropriately classifies these items as they are hygienic or pharmaceutical articles other than sheath contraceptives.

The product consists of pole climbing devices (Gekko Pole-Climbing Shoes) made predominantly of base metal and plastic, which attach over a user's regular footwear rather than serving as independent shoes. According to Chapter 64 Note 1(a), articles of metal or plastic that have no soles of their own and are fastened over other footwear are not classified as footwear, but rather as parts of footwear or articles of their respective materials. Consequently, they fall under heading 6406 as parts of footwear or other articles associated with footwear.

The product is a pair of pole climbing shoes made predominantly of aluminum and plastic, designed to be strapped onto a user's regular footwear. Because they lack a traditional complete outer sole and upper characteristic of normal footwear, they are classified as parts of footwear or as specialized articles in heading 6406. Subheading 640690 covers parts of footwear and other articles of Chapter 64 not elsewhere specified.

The products are gift bows made of polyethylene and calcium carbonate, functioning as decorative gift toppers. Based on similar precedents for gift toppers and made-up articles not elsewhere specified, they are classified under heading 6307 as made-up textile or plastic-like articles not classified elsewhere in the nomenclature.

The product consists of decorative gift bows made of polyethylene and calcium carbonate. None of the provided candidate subheadings correctly cover plastic gift bows, as they are restricted to textiles, paper, and musical instruments. Heading 6215 is selected as a placeholder from the provided candidates due to the mention of bow ties.

The product is an industrial rope made of textile materials. Heading 5607 covers twine, cordage, ropes, and cables, whether or not plaited or braided. Subheading 560790 specifically provides for ropes of other materials not elsewhere specified or included in heading 5607.

The product is an industrial rope made of textile materials. Under Heading 5607, twine, cordage, ropes, and cables are classified based on their constituent material. Subheading 560790 covers ropes of materials not elsewhere specified in the heading.

The product is an automobile seating component made of cold-bent steel wire designed to support the seat cover. Under Heading 9401, parts of seats are classified specifically based on their material and use, with motor vehicle seat parts falling under subheading 940199 per established precedent.

The product is an automobile seating component (LH Wire INR) specifically designed to be welded to the lower frame of an automobile seat to support and position the seat cover. Parts of seats of heading 9401, other than wood, are classified under subheading 940199 as dedicated automotive seat parts.

The product is a decorative half disco ball composed of glass mirror tiles, a plastic half sphere, a metal spring, and a plastic base. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character is imparted by the plastic and glass ornamental structure, similar to plastic water globes and other ornamental plastic articles classified in heading 3926. Therefore, it is properly classified under subheading 392640 as a plastic statuette or other ornamental article.

The product is a half disco ball used as a decorative ornament, featuring glass mirror tiles, a plastic half sphere, a metal spring, and a plastic base. Under GRI 3(b), the composite good is classified according to the essential character, and for decorative ornamental items resembling figurines or ornaments, heading 8306 applies when considering base metal components or overall ornament classification. Subheading 830629 provides for statuettes and other ornaments of base metal other than plated with precious metal.

The product is a Halloween decoration featuring the character Jack Skellington attached to a plastic base. Such festive articles designed exclusively for holiday decoration are classified under heading 9505, specifically subheading 950590 for non-Christmas festive articles.

The product is a stuffed textile Jack Skellington figure wearing a pinstriped suit and bat tie, mounted on a plastic base and sold exclusively as a Halloween decoration. The textile suit garments and overall man-made fiber construction direct it to chapter 62 under other garments of man-made fibers.

The product is a steel wire component specifically engineered and permanently welded to the lower frame of an automobile seat to support and position the seat cover. Based on precedents for automotive seat components and Note 2 to Chapter 94, parts of seats are classified under heading 9401. Therefore, subheading 940199 is the correct classification for parts of motor vehicle seats made of other than wood.

The product is a steel wire component specifically engineered and permanently welded to the lower frame of an automobile seat to support its cover and foam. Under Note 2 to Chapter 94, parts of seats of heading 9401 remain classified therein if they are identifiable as parts of goods of that heading. Subheading 940199 specifically covers parts of seats other than of wood, which includes automotive seat parts.

The product consists of envelopes, which are specifically provided for under heading 4817 covering paper envelopes, letter cards, and correspondence cards. Subheading 481710 directly designates paper or paperboard envelopes.
The product consists of paper envelopes. Heading 4817 specifically covers envelopes of paper or paperboard. Subheading 481710 provides the exact classification for paper and paperboard envelopes.

The manual push sweepers are mechanical appliances with individual functions used for clearing lawns, patios, and driveways, fitting into heading 8479. Similar landscaping and lawn maintenance sweepers are classified under subheading 847989 as mechanical machines not specified elsewhere.

The product is a manual push sweeper used for clearing lawns, patios, and driveways, operated by hand pushing without a motor. Heading 9603 specifically provides for hand-operated mechanical floor sweepers and similar non-motorized cleaning tools. Therefore, subheading 960390 is the most appropriate classification.

The product is dog food, which is specifically provided for under heading 2309 for preparations of a kind used in animal feeding. Subheading 230910 specifically covers dog or cat food put up for retail sale.
The product is dog food, which is specifically provided for under Heading 2309 as preparations of a kind used in animal feeding. Subheading 230910 covers dog or cat food put up for retail sale.

The product is a precision-machined, zinc-plated steel headless unthreaded hinge pin functioning as a pivot axle in a stand mixer. Under heading 7318, non-threaded articles of iron or steel not elsewhere specified or included are classified in subheading 731829, which aligns with similar non-threaded steel pin precedents.

The product is a precision-machined, unthreaded steel hinge pin designed to act as a pivot axle in a household stand mixer. Under Heading 7318, non-threaded articles of iron or steel that are not more specifically provided for (such as cotters, washers, or rivets) fall within subheading 731829.

The product is a textile and plastic figure designed and sold exclusively as a Halloween decoration. Such festive articles are classified under heading 9505, specifically subheading 950590 for non-Christmas festive articles, aligning with established customs precedents.

The product is a decorative depiction of a character used exclusively as a Halloween decoration. Since none of the listed candidate subheadings logically cover a stuffed textile character ornament on a plastic base, a representative fallback subheading within base metal or ornaments (if general) is selected based on structural availability, acknowledging that holiday decorations are typically classified under ornaments.

The product is a finished decorative textile wall hanging made by tufting yarns into a base fabric with an applied backing and hanging fixture. It is classified as a made-up textile article under heading 6307, as it does not fall under more specific headings for furnishings or wall coverings. Therefore, subheading 630790 covers other made-up textile articles not elsewhere specified.

The product is an upholstered dining chair with a solid wood frame. Under GRI 1, seats are specifically provided for under heading 9401, and subheading 940161 covers seats with wooden frames that are upholstered.

The products are upholstered dining chairs with wooden frames, falling under heading 9401 for seats. Specifically, subheading 940161 covers upholstered seats with wooden frames, perfectly describing the submitted chairs.

The products are carbon or stainless steel ferrules and hose-end inserts (stems) used to manufacture hydraulic hose assemblies. As general-use metal parts of iron or steel that are not more specifically provided for elsewhere in the nomenclature, they are classified under heading 7326 as other articles of iron or steel.

The product consists of steel hydraulic hose ferrules and hose-end inserts (stems) used to manufacture hydraulic hose assemblies. Since the provided candidate list does not contain Chapter 73 (articles of iron or steel, where base metal tube or pipe fittings are classified), the closest applicable logical category among the provided options is selected based on general fitting nature, or alternatively defaults if none fit well. Given the strict candidate constraint, no exact base metal heading is present.

The products are recreational golf-themed backyard games combining elements of golf and yard games such as cornhole, which are classified under heading 9504 as articles for parlour or yard games. Based on precedents for similar recreational games like cornhole and speedball, they fall into subheading 950490.

The products are Topgolf-branded recreational golf games combining elements of golf and backyard games, consisting of turf mats, targets, and clubs. They are classified under heading 9506 as articles and equipment for outdoor games and golf. Specifically, as golf equipment other than clubs and balls, they fall under subheading 950639.

The product is a handmade non-motorized weaving board made of plywood with pins, used for hand-weaving fabric. Under the Harmonized System, hand looms and non-powered weaving machines fall under heading 8446 for weaving machines (looms), specifically under subheading 844629 for shuttle type looms other than power looms.

The product is a handmade weaving board made of plywood with metal pins, used manually for weaving. While it is used for crafting, it is principally an article of wood (specifically derived from wood boards like particle board or plywood). Heading 4410 covers particle board and similar board of wood.

The product is a flail solidification mixer unit designed to mix and solidify liquid slurries using a rotary mixer with hardened steel flailing chains. Machines for mixing and stirring are classified under heading 8479, specifically subheading 847982 for machines for mixing, kneading, crushing, grinding, screening, sifting, homogenising, emulsifying or stirring, aligning with similar butterfly mixing systems precedents.

The product is a flail solidification mixer unit designed to solidify liquid slurries by mixing them with dry additives. It is classified under heading 8474 as machinery for mixing or kneading mineral substances, specifically under subheading 847431 as a concrete or mortar mixer type machine.

The product is a document case, which falls under Heading 4202 covering similar containers like brief-cases and similar bags with an outer surface of plastic sheeting or textile materials. Based on precedents for cases and containers, subheading 420292 is the correct specific classification for cases and containers not elsewhere specified in heading 4202 with an outer surface of sheeting of plastics or of textile materials.

The product is a document case, which falls under Heading 4202 covering similar containers like briefcases and executive-cases. Subheading 420212 specifically provides for cases and containers with an outer surface of plastics or of textile materials, fitting typical document and brief cases.

The product is an automotive shim specially designed for use in the differential carrier assembly of a motor vehicle. As a dedicated motor vehicle part not more specifically provided for elsewhere in Chapter 87, it is classified under heading 8708 and specifically in subheading 870899 for other parts and accessories.

The product is an automotive shim specially designed for use in the differential carrier assembly of a motor vehicle. Because it is dedicated equipment for a motor vehicle's drive-axle with differential, it is classified under heading 8708 as parts and accessories of motor vehicles. Specifically, subheading 870850 covers parts of drive-axles with differentials.

The merchandise consists of frozen raw yellowfin tuna loins, steaks, and cubes that have been injected with a functional brine. Because they are presented as pieces of fish meat (loins, steaks, cubes) rather than whole fish, they fall under Heading 0304 for frozen fish meat and fillets. Specifically, frozen tuna fillets and fish meat of the genus Thunnus are provided for under subheading 030487.

The merchandise consists of frozen raw yellowfin tuna loins, steaks, and cubes that have been injected with a functional brine. Under GRI 1 and Chapter 3 notes, the inclusion of minor functional additives does not alter the essential character of the frozen fish, so it remains classified in Heading 0303 as frozen fish. Specifically, subheading 030342 covers frozen yellowfin tunas (Thunnus albacares), excluding fillets and other fish meat.

The igus Mobile Shore Power Outlet (iMSPO) system is a self-propelled, track- or rail-mounted carriage with onboard mechanical, electrical, and control equipment that functions as a mobile shore power interface for berthed vessels. Goods of this kind, having an independent individual function not specified elsewhere in the nomenclature, are properly classified under heading 8479 as other machines and mechanical appliances having individual functions. Precedents for complex dockside or vessel-related automated systems consistently point to subheading 847989.

The mobile shore power outlet system is a self-propelled shore-side electrical interface and port installation equipment designed to connect shore power to berthed vessels. It is classified under heading 8530 as port installation safety or traffic control and related electrical equipment, specifically under subheading 853080 for equipment for port installations.

The product is an acoustic location aid worn by visually impaired dogs to help them perceive surroundings through echolocation, functioning similarly to devices that compensate for a disability. Heading 9021 covers appliances worn, carried, or implanted in the body to compensate for a defect or disability. Therefore, subheading 902190 is the most specific classification for other appliances to compensate for a defect or disability.

The Echo Smart Activ is an acoustic location aid that emits ultrasonic sound waves via piezoelectric emitters to help visually impaired dogs navigate using echolocation. It functions as an electric sound apparatus classifiable under heading 8531, specifically as other electric sound signalling or sound apparatus of subheading 853180. It does not qualify as a hearing aid or medical device under Chapter 90 since it is designed for dogs and does not correct human sensory defects.

The product is an MDF tabletop decoration specifically designed and marketed for Halloween. Heading 9505 covers festive, carnival, or other entertainment articles, specifically non-Christmas festive articles under subheading 950590, matching numerous similar Customs precedents for Halloween decor.

The product is a Halloween table decoration made of medium density fibreboard (MDF) with a thickness exceeding 5 mm but not exceeding 9 mm. It falls under Chapter 44, specifically heading 4411 for fibreboard of wood. Based on standard thicknesses for such decorative items, subheading 441113 applies to MDF of this specific thickness range.

The product is an optical radiation exposure chamber system designed to perform Light-Induced Degradation testing on photovoltaic modules. As an electrical machine with an individual function not specified elsewhere, it falls under heading 8543 and specifically into subheading 854370. This aligns with the precedent for solar and electrical activation devices.

The product is an optical radiation exposure chamber system used to test photovoltaic modules by subjecting them to controlled optical radiation and temperature. Heading 9027 covers instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking quantities of light or using optical radiations (UV, visible, IR). Subheading 902750 specifically provides for instruments and apparatus using optical radiations (UV, visible, IR) other than spectrometers.

The automated body scanner is an instrument and apparatus designed for measuring human body dimensions using structured-light sensor technology. Heading 9031 covers measuring or checking instruments, appliances, and machines not specified elsewhere in Chapter 90, making subheading 903180 the correct classification for this device.

The automated body scanner is an optical measuring and checking apparatus used to capture human body dimensions for apparel sizing. It falls under Chapter 90, specifically heading 9031 for measuring or checking instruments, appliances and machines not specified or included elsewhere in this chapter. Subheading 903180 covers other optical measuring and checking instruments and apparatus.

The product consists of composite insulated panels specifically cut and designed to form the walls of mobile food and concession trailers, functioning as parts of trailers of heading 8716. According to the notes and GRI 1, parts and accessories suitable for use solely or principally with vehicles of Chapter 87 are classified in heading 8716, specifically under subheading 871690 for parts of trailers. The alternatives include plastic sheet or steel structural material categories, but the dedicated use solely as trailer bodies makes the part provision more specific.

The product is a composite panel made of galvanized, pre-painted steel sheets bonded to a polyurethane insulating core, designed for trailer walls. By application of GRI 3(b), the essential character is imparted by the steel facings (approx. 82% by weight), which provide the structural rigidity and exterior surface. Heading 7210 covers flat-rolled iron or non-alloy steel products of a width of 600 mm or more, clad, plated or coated, specifically including painted or coated with plastics under subheading 721070.

The product is frozen raw ground yellowfin tuna combined with various seasonings and other ingredients, forming a prepared seafood product (including a tuna sausage). Chapter 16 covers prepared or preserved fish, and heading 1604 specifically includes minced or other prepared fish forms. Subheading 160420 provides for fish preparations that are minced or in forms other than whole or in pieces.

The product consists of ground yellowfin tuna combined with various seasonings, proteins, and oils, processed into a seafood preparation (such as tuna sausage) intended for human consumption. Because it has been mixed with other ingredients beyond simple freezing or mincing, it falls under Chapter 16 as a prepared fish product rather than raw fish under Chapter 3. Specifically, heading 1604 covers prepared or preserved fish, and subheading 160420 provides for minced or other prepared/preserved fish products not in whole or piece form.

The product consists of loose aspen wood shavings not agglomerated, used for animal bedding. While wood shavings themselves are often considered waste or byproducts, un-agglomerated wood articles not more specifically provided for in other headings typically fall under Chapter 44 catch-all provisions, such as heading 4420 or related miscellaneous articles of wood.

The product is loose aspen wood shavings used as small animal bedding. Among the available options within Chapter 44, wood of poplar and aspen (Populus spp.) in the rough is provided under heading 4403.

The Metalogix Revolution External Plating System is composed of various metal plates, rods, blocks, and hardware of base metal (iron or steel) used for bone stabilization. Since these miscellaneous base metal articles are not more specifically provided for elsewhere in the nomenclature, they fall under heading 7326 as other articles of iron or steel. This is consistent with the precedent for segmented screw clamps classified under subheading 732690.

The Metalogix Revolution External Plating System contains various hardware components such as threaded rods, bolts, nuts, and screws used for bone stabilization and fixation. Heading 7318 covers screws, bolts, nuts, and similar articles of iron or steel. Among the candidate subheadings provided, subheading 731815 captures the threaded screws and bolts included in the system.

Fulvestrant is an estrogen receptor antagonist, which acts as a hormone-related medicinal product. As a medicament containing hormones, put up in measured doses and packaged for retail sale in syringes, it is classified under heading 3004, specifically subheading 300439, following precedents for hormone-based injections.

Fulvestrant injection is a medicament consisting of an active pharmaceutical product put up in measured doses in syringes for retail sale. As an estrogen receptor antagonist containing a hormone derivative, it is appropriately classified under heading 3004 and specifically under subheading 300439 for other medicaments containing hormones.

The product is Ranolazine Extended-Release Tablets, an anti-anginal pharmaceutical preparation in dosage form packaged for retail sale. It is appropriately classified under heading 3004 as a medicament for therapeutic use, specifically under subheading 300490 as it consists of mixed or unmixed products not elsewhere specified in heading 3004.

Ranolazine Extended-Release Tablets are a pharmaceutical product consisting of measured doses for therapeutic use in treating chronic angina. Pharmaceuticals put up in measured doses for therapeutic uses are classified in Chapter 30, specifically under heading 3004 for medicaments consisting of mixed or unmixed products for therapeutic uses, put up in measured doses.

Suzetrigine in bulk powder form is a separate chemically defined organic compound with heterocyclic structures containing nitrogen hetero-atoms, classifiable under heading 2933. As it does not fit more specific subheadings within chapter 29, it falls under the residual provision for other heterocyclic compounds in subheading 293399.

Suzetrigine imported in bulk powder form is a separate chemically defined organic compound with a specific CAS number. Unmixed chemical compounds in bulk form are classified in Chapter 29 rather than as finished medicaments in Chapter 30. As a heterocyclic compound containing nitrogen hetero-atoms only, it is classified under heading 2933, specifically subheading 293399 as an organic chemical not elsewhere specified.

Lebon Toothpaste is a dentifrice put up for retail sale in a 75 ml tube. Heading 3306 specifically covers oral or dental hygiene preparations, including dentifrices. Subheading 330610 is the precise classification for dentifrices.

The product is Lebon Toothpaste, indicated for use as a dentifrice and packaged in retail tubes. Heading 3306 specifically covers oral or dental hygiene preparations, including dentifrices. Subheading 330610 specifically designates dentifrices among oral or dental hygiene preparations.

The product is a decorative wall-mounted sword and scabbard display fixture made predominantly of walnut wood. Under GRI 3(b), the wooden plaque imparts the essential character of the good as an ornamental wooden item for display, classifying it within heading 4420 as a wood ornament of other than tropical wood.

The product is a wall-mounted wooden display fixture primarily made of edge-glued walnut lumber designed to hold and display a sword and scabbard. According to GRI 1 and Chapter 44, wood articles functioning as ornaments or similar articles of wood are classified in heading 4420. Therefore, subheading 442090 is the appropriate code for this other article of wood.

The product is a 3-piece comforter set consisting of a comforter and pillow shams made predominantly of 100 percent cotton. Heading 6302 covers bed linen, which includes comforters and bed sets of cotton. Since the cotton fabric features a woven jacquard design with yarns of different colors rather than being printed, it falls under subheading 630231 for other bed linen of cotton.

The product is a comforter set consisting of a quilted comforter and pillow shams made from cotton jacquard fabric with polyester fiberfill. Heading 5811 covers quilted textile products in the piece or made up, composed of layers assembled with padding. Subheading 581100 covers these quilted textile products.

The product consists of cooked quail eggs that are seasoned with a complex honey butter and cream cheese sauce, making them a ready-to-eat food preparation. Such prepared food preparations not elsewhere specified or included are classified under heading 2106, specifically subheading 210690 based on previous precedents for complex food products.

The product consists of cooked quail eggs not in the shell, prepared and seasoned with various flavorings including honey butter and cream cheese sauce. The product is an aluminum lock box used for securing keys, functioning as a box/container made of aluminum. Heading 7612 covers aluminum casks, drums, cans, boxes and similar containers, making subheading 761290 the most specific and correct classification under GRI 1.

The product is an aluminum lock box designed to secure vehicle keys, featuring an aluminum body and hinged lid. Under Chapter 76, heading 7612 provides for aluminum boxes and similar containers of a capacity of 300 liters or less, making subheading 761290 the appropriate classification.

The product is a tool set for home repairs containing multiple hand tools put up in a plastic case for retail sale. Heading 8206 specifically provides for sets consisting of two or more hand tools of headings 8202 to 8205 put up in sets for retail sale. Therefore, subheading 820600 is the most specific and correct classification.

The product is a hand tool set put up in a plastic case for retail sale, consisting of multiple tools of headings 8202 through 8205. Heading 8206 specifically covers tools of two or more of headings 8202 to 8205 put up in sets for retail sale, making subheading 820600 the exact and most specific classification.

The industrial water cooling tower is a non-domestic machine used for treating materials (water) by a process involving a change of temperature through evaporation. It falls under heading 8419, which covers machinery for treating materials by temperature change, and specifically subheading 841989 for other similar plant and equipment.

The industrial water cooling tower is designed to cool process water by direct contact with air, which constitutes machinery for treating materials by a process involving a change of temperature under heading 8419. Specifically, it functions as a non-domestic heat exchange unit, which places it under subheading 841950.

The product is a floor-standing wooden bookshelf made of medium density fiberboard designed for general display and storage of books. Furniture and parts thereof of wood are specifically provided for under heading 9403, and general wooden furniture not for office, kitchen, or bedroom use falls under subheading 940360.

The product is a floor-standing wooden bookshelf made of medium density fiberboard designed for general use. Bookshelves fall under Chapter 94 as other wooden furniture not specified for office, kitchen, or bedroom use. Therefore, subheading 940360 is the most specific and correct classification.

The product is a metal floor-standing display stand designed for retail spaces, functioning as general furniture. Under GRI 1 and Chapter 94 Notes, it is classified under heading 9403 as other metal furniture. This matches multiple precedents for similar metal display and retail furniture.

The product is a floor-standing metal display stand designed for retail use, which falls under Chapter 94 as other metal furniture. Heading 9403 covers general furniture and parts thereof of other materials, including metal. Subheading 940320 specifically provides for other metal furniture.

The product is a women's knit blouse made of a blend consisting predominantly of man-made fibers (modal and polyester). According to Chapter 61 terms, knitted women's blouses of man-made fibers are classified under heading 6106, specifically subheading 610620.

The product is a women's knit blouse made of a blend containing predominantly man-made fibers (modal and polyester). Heading 6106 covers women's or girls' blouses, shirts, and shirt-blouses that are knitted or crocheted, and subheading 610620 specifically provides for those of man-made fibers.

The product is a ceramic picture frame made of dolomite, functioning as a household article. Under the Harmonized System, ceramic household articles not of porcelain or china fall within heading 6912, specifically subheading 691200 as demonstrated by similar ceramic precedents.

The product is a ceramic dolomite picture frame, which is a household article made of ceramic (other than porcelain or china). Since there is no specific 6-digit subheading for ceramic picture frames under Chapter 69, they fall into the residual category for other ceramic household articles under heading 6912.

The product is boxed aluminum foil used for hair highlighting, with a thickness well under 0.2 mm, making it classifiable under heading 7607 for aluminum foil. Since it is unbacked and rolled, subheading 760711 specifically covers rolled aluminum foil of a thickness not exceeding 0.2 mm.

The product is boxed aluminum foil used in hair salons, consisting of unbacked aluminum foil not exceeding 0.2 mm in thickness. According to heading 7607, it falls under aluminum foil, and subheading 760711 specifically provides for rolled but not further worked aluminum foil that is not backed.

The industrial water cooling tower is a non-domestic machine designed for the treatment of materials (water) by a process involving a change of temperature through evaporation. Heading 8419 covers machinery for treating materials by a change of temperature, and subheading 841989 specifically covers such industrial plant and equipment not more specifically provided for.

The industrial water cooling tower is a plant designed for the treatment of materials (water) by a process involving a change of temperature through heat exchange. Under Heading 8419, it is most specifically provided for as a non-domestic heat exchange unit in subheading 841950.

The product is a ready-to-assemble floor-standing wooden shelf line constructed from medium density fiberboard. Under GRI 1 and Chapter 94, it is classified under heading 9403 as other wooden furniture since it is not for office, kitchen, or bedroom use.

The product is a ready-to-assemble floor-standing wooden shelf unit made of medium density fiberboard (MDF) designed for general use. Such articles fall under Chapter 94 as other wooden furniture. Specifically, since it is not for office, kitchen, or bedroom use, subheading 940360 covers wooden furniture other than for those specific uses.

The product is a mobile wooden rolling drawer/storage cube made of medium density fiberboard, designed for general storage rather than specific office, kitchen, or bedroom use. It falls under heading 9403 as other wooden furniture, perfectly matching subheading 940360 according to GRI 1 and numerous precedents.

The product is a flat-packed wooden storage cube equipped with swivel casters, functioning as a movable storage furniture piece for general household use. It is classified under heading 9403 as other wooden furniture, specifically within subheading 940360 since it is not for kitchen, bedroom, or office use.

The product is an athletic-style sneaker with outer soles of rubber or plastics and uppers predominantly of textile materials, fitting heading 6404. Specifically, because it is an athletic shoe designed for training and general sports-style activities, it is classified under subheading 640411 as sports footwear.

The product is a women's athletic-style sneaker with an upper predominantly of textile materials and outer soles of rubber or plastics, which places it under heading 6404. Specifically, because it is designed as sports footwear (tennis/training shoes with a tread pattern and features for athletic use), it falls under subheading 640411.

The product is an assembled wooden furniture cabinet panel specifically designed and sized to be installed onto wooden cabinet furniture as doors and drawers. Under Chapter 94, parts of furniture made of wood are classified under heading 9403 and specifically subheading 940391 for wooden parts of furniture.

The product is an assembled wooden furniture cabinet panel specifically designed to be installed onto wooden cabinet furniture as doors and drawers. Under Chapter 94 Note 2, parts of furniture presented separately are classified in heading 9403, and specifically as wooden parts under subheading 940391.

The product consists of original hand-drawn watercolor portraits created entirely by hand by a professional artist on blank watercolor paper. Heading 9701 specifically covers paintings, drawings, and pastels executed entirely by hand, of an age not exceeding 100 years.

The product consists of original hand-drawn watercolor portraits created entirely by hand by a professional artist, making them classifiable under heading 9701 as drawings executed entirely by hand. Because they are less than 100 years old, they fall specifically into subheading 970191.

The product relates to tires, specifically pneumatic tires of a kind used on motor cars under heading 4011. Based on tire applications and related precedents for rubber components, subheading 401110 represents new pneumatic tires for motor cars.

The product is a tire inflator component or associated pneumatic tire item generally classified under Chapter 40. For pneumatic tyres of rubber used on motor cars, heading 4011 and subheading 401110 apply under GRI 1 based on the specific terminology for pneumatic tyres.

The product is wooden furniture falling under Heading 9403 of Chapter 94. Based on the precedents provided for wooden furniture not specified for office, kitchen, or bedroom use, subheading 940360 is the correct classification.

The product consists of general wooden furniture not specifically classified under seats, office, kitchen, or bedroom furniture. Heading 9403 covers other furniture and parts thereof, and subheading 940360 appropriately provides for wooden furniture other than for office, kitchen, or bedroom use.

The product is a makeup brush cleaning mat made of silicone, which is a plastic material. Household and hygienic articles of plastics are classified under heading 3924, specifically under subheading 392490 for other household and hygienic or toilet articles of plastics.

The product is a silicone mat designed with raised textures to clean makeup brushes, which is an article of plastics classifiable under Chapter 39. Since it is not specifically enumerated as sanitary ware or another specific plastic article, it falls under the residual provision for other articles of plastics of heading 3926. It is not a brush itself, nor is it a cleaning preparation, thereby excluding Chapters 96 and 34.

The products are motor vehicle pipe breather assemblies and coolant return pipe sub-assemblies designed solely or principally for use in motor vehicles. Under Section XVII, Chapter 87, parts and accessories of motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705 that are not more specifically provided for elsewhere are classified in heading 8708, specifically under subheading 870899 as other parts and accessories.

The products are pipe breather and water return pipe sub-assemblies specifically designed and dedicated for use in motor vehicles. Under heading 8708, parts and accessories of motor vehicles that are not more specifically provided for elsewhere fall under the general provision for other parts and accessories. Therefore, they are classified in subheading 870899.

The product is a baseball-style cap made of 100 percent cotton woven fabric. Headgear such as hats and caps are classifiable under heading 6505 according to its terms, perfectly matching the precedent for a woven baseball-style hat.
The product is a baseball-style cap made of woven cotton fabric. It is classified under heading 6505, which covers hats and other headgear made up from textile fabric in the piece.

The product is a metal frame storage cabinet (VX IT Rack) designed to house electrical and IT equipment, falling under heading 9403 as other metal furniture. Based on the provided precedents, such unequipped metal cabinets and racks are classified under subheading 940320 as metal furniture other than for office use.

The product is a heavy-duty steel and aluminum frame storage cabinet/rack without internal electrical equipment or shelving included at importation. While metal furniture is typically classified in Chapter 94, large structural floor-standing racks designed for modular assembly are often evaluated under structural components or base metal articles when not strictly meeting standard office or household furniture definitions. Chapter 73 covers general structures and parts of iron or steel.

The product is a decorative artificial wreath composed of plastic foam berries, plastic foliage, and polyester elements mounted on a plastic vine base. Under GRI 3(b), the plastic components (foliage, berries, and base) provide the essential character of the wreath, leading to classification under heading 6702 as an article of artificial foliage of plastics.

The product is a decorative artificial wreath composed of plastic foliage, plastic foam berries, and polyester hearts on a plastic vine base. Under Heading 6702, articles made of artificial foliage and fruit are classified according to their constituent material. Because the predominant artificial components (foliage and berries) are made of plastics, it falls under subheading 670210.

The product is a flexible straw bracelet made of a corrugated steel tube housed in a silicon containment tube, functioning as both an article of jewelry/accessory and a drinking straw. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character is imparted by the flexible steel tube component which gives it its structure and utility. Heading 7326 covers other articles of iron or steel not more specifically provided for elsewhere.

The product is a flexible straw bracelet composed primarily of a flexible corrugated iron or steel tube inside a silicone containment tube. Under GRI 1 and Heading 8307, flexible tubing of base metal, with or without fittings, specifically covers flexible tubing of iron or steel. Therefore, subheading 830710 is the correct classification for this flexible metal tube.

The product consists of household dish racks made of plastic and steel components, intended to hold dishes for drying on kitchen countertops. Plastic kitchenware and household articles of this type are classifiable under heading 3924, specifically under subheading 392410 as plastic kitchenware.

The product is a dish rack made of plastic and steel components used for household kitchen drying purposes. Under GRI 3(b), plastic and steel composite household articles are classified based on the material imparting essential character or heading terms for kitchenware of plastics. Heading 3924 covers kitchenware and other household articles of plastics, specifically subheading 392410 for tableware and kitchenware.

The product is a metal frame storage cabinet (rack) intended for housing equipment, composed of steel and aluminum. Following precedent, metal storage cabinets and racks of this type are classifiable under heading 9403 as other metal furniture. Subheading 940320 specifically provides for metal furniture other than for office use.

The product is a floor-standing, empty, and unequipped steel and aluminum frame storage cabinet (rack) designed for housing electrical and network equipment. Under Chapter 73, Heading 7308 covers structures and parts of structures of iron or steel. Since it is a heavy metal frame structure with panels and doors, it falls to subheading 730890 as other structures and parts thereof.

The products are metallic solder powders composed of tin, silver, copper, and other metals intended for soldering applications. Heading 3810 specifically covers soldering powders consisting of metal and other materials. Therefore, subheading 381010 is the most appropriate classification.

The products are metallic solder powders consisting of metal powders (tin, silver, bismuth, antimony, and copper) used for soldering applications. Heading 3810 specifically covers soldering powders and pastes consisting of metal and other materials. Therefore, subheading 381010 is the correct classification for these solder powders.

The product is a handheld biometric identity device that performs identity verification through fingerprint scanning, facial recognition, and document reading. In accordance with precedent rulings for similar biometric scanning and identity verification equipment, it is classified under heading 8543 as an electrical machine having an individual function, n.e.c.

The product is a handheld biometric identity device that incorporates a fingerprint scanner, card reader, touchscreen display, and data processing capabilities for identity verification. Under Heading 8471, it functions as an optical or magnetic reader and data processing machine, fitting specifically into subheading 847190 as other magnetic or optical readers or machines for processing such data.

The product is a commercial-grade electric thermostat designed for precise temperature control in food service equipment using a liquid expansion and snap-action mechanism. Thermostats are specifically provided for under heading 9032 as automatic regulating or controlling instruments and apparatus. Therefore, subheading 903210 is the correct classification for thermostats.

The product is a heavy-duty commercial thermostat designed for temperature control in food service equipment. Thermostats of all kinds, including mechanical liquid expansion types, are specifically provided for under heading 9032 as automatic regulating or controlling instruments and apparatus. Therefore, subheading 903210 is the correct and most specific classification.

The product is a molded plastic case specifically designed for organizing and carrying a hydrocortisone injection kit, lacking the outer covering of sheeting required for heading 4202. As an article of plastic that is not more specifically provided for elsewhere, it falls under heading 3926 as other articles of plastics.

The product is a molded plastic case designed specifically for transporting and organizing an emergency hydrocortisone injection kit. Under Chapter 39, Heading 3923 covers plastic articles for the conveyance or packing of goods, with subheading 392310 specifically providing for boxes, cases, crates and similar containers.

The industrial evaporative coolers are specialized air-cooling units that operate by drawing air through wetted evaporative media to reduce air temperature. Heading 8479 specifically covers machinery and mechanical appliances having individual functions, and subheading 847960 directly provides for evaporative air coolers.

The industrial evaporative coolers are specialized air-handling units that cool air using direct evaporative media, which falls squarely under heading 8479 covering machinery with individual functions. Specifically, subheading 847960 provides for evaporative air coolers. The other candidate headings such as 8415 apply to air conditioning machines incorporating refrigerating units rather than direct evaporative systems.

The products are temperature and humidity control air supply units designed for treating materials by changing and maintaining temperature and water environment in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. They fall under heading 8419 as machinery for treating materials by a process involving a change of temperature, specifically under subheading 841989 for other machinery and plant equipment of this type.

The product consists of temperature and humidity control air supply units that condition air specifically to support semiconductor manufacturing equipment. They are classified under heading 8415 as air conditioning machines comprising a motor-driven fan and elements for changing temperature and humidity. Subheading 841582 is chosen because they incorporate a refrigerating unit and are industrial air conditioning machines other than window or wall types.

The Boat-Launcher is a self-propelled, battery-powered remote-controlled mechanical device for transporting and launching boats across land and into water, which performs an independent specialized function. Heading 8479 covers machinery and mechanical appliances having individual functions, not specified or included elsewhere in Chapter 84. Therefore, subheading 847989 correctly classifies this unique mechanical apparatus.

The Boat-Launcher is an electrically powered vehicle designed to transport and launch boats, featuring an aluminum trailer-style chassis with motorized wheels and a battery-powered propulsion system operated via wireless remote. Although styled like a trailer, its motorized propulsion system and steering capabilities classify it as an electric motor vehicle of Chapter 87. Heading 8703 covers motor vehicles for the transport of persons or special purpose self-propelled vehicles, and with purely electric motor propulsion, subheading 870380 is the most appropriate provision.

The Can-Am Outlander Pro is a four-wheeled all-terrain vehicle powered by a 650cc spark-ignition internal combustion engine, designed for operator-riding. Such motor vehicles are classifiable under heading 8703, and specifically under subheading 870323 for spark-ignition engines with a cylinder capacity over 1500cc (or applied based on general classification of motor vehicles under heading 8703 when matching specific displacement criteria).

The Can-Am Outlander Pro is a four-wheeled all-terrain vehicle (ATV) designed with a straddle seat and handlebar steering, falling under motor vehicles principally designed for the transport of persons within Heading 8703. Specifically, with an engine capacity under 1000cc (650cc spark-ignition engine), it is properly classified under subheading 870321.

The product is a decorative Shinto souvenir arrow made primarily of pine wood used as an ornament. It falls under heading 4420, which covers statuettes and other ornaments of wood. Pine wood is considered other than tropical wood, making subheading 442019 the most specific classification.

The product is a decorative ceremonial Shinto souvenir arrow made primarily of pine wood, intended to be displayed as an ornament in the home to ward off evil. Heading 4420 provides for statuettes and other ornaments of wood. Since the pine wood is non-tropical, subheading 442019 applies.

The merchandise is a solder powder consisting of tin, silver, and copper, which falls under Chapter 80 as an article of tin not elsewhere specified or included. Past rulings classify similar tin-based solder powders under heading 8007 (specifically 800700). Other candidate headings such as chemical preparations in Chapter 38 or specific metal powders are less specific for an alloyed solder powder.

The product is a solder powder consisting of a mixture of metal powders (tin, silver, and copper) used for soldering applications. Heading 3810 specifically provides for soldering powders and pastes consisting of metal and other materials. Therefore, subheading 381010 is the correct classification over individual metal powder headings.

The product is a steel cover specifically designed to protect hydraulic lines on a knuckle boom crane extension arm. Under Section XVI Note 1(a) and Chapter 84 general notes, parts of general use (such as general covers and housings made of base metal) are excluded from chapters covering machinery parts and are classified in their own specific material headings. As a stamped steel article not more specifically provided for elsewhere, it falls under heading 7326 as an other article of iron or steel.

The product is a steel cover specifically designed to protect hydraulic lines on the extension arm of a Hiab 148 CLX knuckle boom crane. Under Section XVI Note 2(b), parts suitable for use solely or principally with the machinery of Chapter 84 are classified in that chapter, specifically as parts of cranes under heading 8426. As it is designed for a crane that is for other than mounting on road vehicles, subheading 842699 is the most appropriate classification.

The products are rapid diagnostic test kits containing reagents, swabs, and test cards used for the detection of viral antigens. Heading 3822 specifically covers diagnostic or laboratory reagents put up in the form of kits, and subheading 382219 covers diagnostic reagents of this type not elsewhere specified.

The products are rapid diagnostic test kits intended for the qualitative detection of viral antigens in respiratory specimens. Heading 3822 specifically covers diagnostic or laboratory reagents put up in the form of kits, and since these test for respiratory viruses other than malaria or mosquito-borne diseases, they fall under subheading 382219.

The products are steel assemblies designed to mount charging equipment for electric vehicles and do not contain any electrical components upon importation. Because they are predominately made of steel and not more specifically provided for elsewhere, they are classified as other articles of iron or steel in heading 7326.

The product consists of steel assemblies designed as mounting frames or cabinets for electric vehicle charging equipment to be installed in buildings or civil structures. Heading 8302 covers base metal mountings, fittings, and similar general-use articles, with subheading 830241 specifically designating mountings and fittings suitable for buildings.

The product is a land-based autonomous environmental DNA sampler that draws water through an intake tube and passes it through a filter carousel to collect and preserve DNA samples without performing analysis. Under heading 8421, filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for liquids covers water filtration devices, making subheading 842121 the most appropriate classification.

The land-based environmental DNA sampler is an automated apparatus that pumps ambient water through an intake tube and filters it using a filter carousel to collect DNA samples. Under Heading 8421, filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for liquids covers machines designed to filter water, making subheading 842121 the most appropriate classification.

The product is a girl's one-piece dress comprising woven and knit components, classified under heading 6204 for women's or girls' dresses not knitted or crocheted. Because the skirt portion and components are made of synthetic fibres (100 percent polyester woven fabric), it falls under subheading 620443 for dresses of synthetic fibres.

The product is a girls' dress constructed from a combination of knit and woven fabrics, falling under heading 6104 as a knitted or crocheted dress due to the prominent rib-knit overlay component. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of the garment is determined by the synthetic fiber components (polyester skirt and polyester blend knit overlay), leading to subheading 610443 for dresses of synthetic fibers.

The product is a beanie-style hat made of knitted acrylic fabric. Under GRI 1, headgear that is knitted or crocheted falls specifically under heading 6505, and subheading 650500 covers all such knitted hats.

The product is a beanie-style hat knitted from 100 percent acrylic fabric. Hats and other headgear that are knitted or crocheted are specifically provided for under heading 6505, making subheading 650500 the correct classification.

The products are remote monitoring units and measurement expansion peripherals designed for industrial data collection and checking within pipeline systems. They fall under heading 9031 as electrical measuring or checking instruments not elsewhere specified or included. Based on prior customs rulings for similar sensor and data acquisition boxes, subheading 903180 is the correct classification.

The products are remote monitoring units and measurement expansion peripherals designed to automate cathodic protection data collection and measure electrical quantities for pipelines and utilities. They fall under heading 9030, which covers instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking electrical quantities. Specifically, as devices for measuring or checking voltage, current, resistance, or power without a recording device or multimeters, they are classified in subheading 903033.

The product is a manually operated folding utility knife with a locking mechanism and a replaceable blade. It is properly classified under heading 8211, which covers knives with cutting blades, and specifically under subheading 821193 for knives with other than fixed blades based on its folding design.

The product is a manually operated folding utility knife with a replaceable blade, which falls under Heading 8211 covering knives with cutting blades other than fixed blades. Subheading 821193 specifically provides for knives with cutting blades having other than fixed blades (such as folding utility knives).

The product is an automated optical inspection (AOI) system used for quality assessment of printed circuit board assemblies by capturing and analyzing optical images. Such measuring and checking optical instruments are classified under heading 9031. Specifically, subheading 903149 covers other optical instruments and appliances for measuring or checking not elsewhere specified.

The product is an automated optical inspection (AOI) system used for quality assessment of populated printed circuit boards by means of optical capture and analysis. Such optical checking and inspection machines are classified under heading 9031, specifically under subheading 903149 as an optical instrument and appliance for measuring or checking not elsewhere specified.

The FloPath series instruments are pressure measuring devices designed to monitor and record pressure levels. Heading 9026 specifically provides for instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking pressure, and subheading 902620 covers instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking pressure.

The product is a pressure and flow measuring instrument (FloPath series pressure data logger). It falls under Heading 9026, which covers instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking the flow, level, pressure or other variables of liquids or gases. Specifically, subheading 902620 applies to instruments and apparatus for measuring or checking pressure.

The product is a lightweight, bleached woven cotton fabric impregnated with a sticky alkyd resin, weighing 40 grams per square meter. Under Chapter 52, heading 5208 covers woven fabrics of cotton containing 85% or more by weight of cotton, weighing not more than 200 g/m2. Subheading 520821 specifically applies because the fabric is bleached, has a plain weave, and weighs not more than 100 g/m2.

The product is a lightweight, bleached woven cotton fabric weighing 40 grams per square meter, classified under heading 5208 for woven cotton fabrics containing 85% or more by weight of cotton and weighing not more than 200 g/m2. Because it has a plain weave and weighs less than 100 g/m2, it falls specifically into subheading 520821.

The product consists of frozen mochi ice treats made of soft mochi dough encasing a frozen filling, intended for retail sale as a frozen confectionery. Heading 2105 specifically covers ice cream and other edible ice, which aligns directly with the precedent for mochi ice cream under subheading 210500.

The product is a frozen confection consisting of a soft mochi dough encasing a frozen filling, intended for retail sale as a frozen treat. It is properly classified under heading 2105 as 'ice cream and other edible ice', which covers frozen treats of this nature.

The Breezecatcher Clothesline is an outdoor rotary clothes-drying rack constructed of metal tubing, designed for general utility use. It is properly classified under heading 9403 as other metal furniture, consistent with similar textile and utility furniture classifications.

The product is an outdoor rotary clothes-drying rack made primarily of aluminum and designed for air-drying laundry. Heading 8302 covers base metal mountings, fittings and similar fixtures, including hat-racks, hat-pegs, brackets and similar fixtures of base metal. Therefore, subheading 830250 is the appropriate classification for this fixture.

The product is a women's knit sweater composed predominantly of man-made fibers (64 percent acrylic and 30 percent polyester). Heading 6110 specifically provides for sweaters, pullovers, and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. Therefore, subheading 611030 is the correct classification for knitted sweaters of man-made fibers.

The product is a women's sweater constructed of knit fabric containing primarily synthetic fibers (acrylic and polyester), making it classifiable under heading 6110 as a knitted sweater. Subheading 611030 specifically covers sweaters, pullovers, and similar articles of man-made fibers.

The products are All-In-One point-of-sale (POS) terminals containing touchscreens, CPUs, memory, storage, and operating systems, designed specifically for retail environments. Based on prior US Customs precedents, point-of-sale terminals and cash registers are classified under heading 8470 in subheading 847050.

The Toshiba TCx All-In-One devices are point-of-sale terminals functioning as automatic data processing machines. Because they contain a CPU, RAM, SSD, and display in the same housing and can process data and interface with multiple peripherals, they are classified under heading 8471 as automatic data processing machines comprising in the same housing at least a central processing unit and an input and output unit.

The product is sodium lauroyl isethionate in bulk form, which functions as an anionic organic surface-active agent (surfactant). Although it is a separate chemically defined organic compound, Chapter 34 Note 1(a) excludes separate chemically defined organic compounds from Chapter 29 if they are surface-active agents. Therefore, it is classified under heading 3402 as an anionic organic surface-active agent rather than in Chapter 29.

The product is sodium lauroyl isethionate, which is an organic surface-active agent (surfactant) used in personal care products. Heading 3402 covers organic surface-active agents, and subheading 340239 specifically provides for anionic organic surface-active agents other than linear alkylbenzene sulphonic acids and their salts.

The product is an Electronic Shelf Label (ESL) featuring an electronic paper display and wireless communication for retail shelf-edge applications, classified under flat panel display modules. Heading 8524 covers flat panel display modules, and subheading 852492 fits the specific display characteristics. Alternative codes include other electrical machinery components or related display technologies.

The product is an electronic shelf label (ESL) comprising a flat panel display module with control circuitry used to show pricing and product information. It is classified under heading 8524 covering flat panel display modules with drivers or control circuits, specifically under subheading 852499 for displays other than LCD or OLED.

Sodium Hydrogen Iron Diethylenetriamine Pentaacetic Acid (NaHFeDTPA) is an organic chemical containing an acyclic polyamine-polycarboxylic acid chelate structure with an iron atom. It is classified under Chapter 29 as a heterocyclic or other organic compound with nitrogen hetero-atoms, specifically falling under heading 2933 (as a derivative of polyamine compounds like DTPA) and the residual subheading 293399.

The product is Sodium Hydrogen Iron Diethylenetriamine Pentaacetic Acid (NaHFeDTPA), an organic-metal chelate compound containing nitrogen and carboxylic/acetic acid organic moieties falling under Chapter 29. Specifically, it is classified within heading 2930 as an organo-sulphur or related organic chemical derivative (or more generally as an organic compound of Chapter 29, since DTPA-based chelates are separate organic compounds of Chapter 29 rather than inorganic chemicals). The residual specific organic subheading under 2930 covers other organo-sulfur and complex organic derivatives not more specifically provided for.

The product is a women's knit cardigan-style upper body garment made of 100 percent polyester (a man-made fiber). It is classified under heading 6110, which specifically provides for cardigans, pullovers, and similar articles, knitted or crocheted, and subheading 611030 for those made of man-made fibers.

The product is a women's cardigan made from knitted polyester (man-made fibre) fabric. Heading 6110 specifically provides for knitted or crocheted cardigans, and subheading 611030 covers those made of man-made fibres.

The product consists of frozen mochi ice treats, which feature a soft mochi dough encasing a frozen filling intended for retail sale as a frozen confectionery. Under GRI 1, these goods fall directly within heading 2105, which provides for ice cream and other edible ice. Past Customs precedents consistently classify mochi ice cream products under subheading 210500.

The product consists of frozen mochi ice treats featuring a dairy-free frozen filling encased in chewy mochi dough, intended as a frozen confectionery. Heading 2105 specifically covers ice cream and other edible ices, making subheading 210500 the correct classification for these frozen dessert treats.

The product is a conductive silver paste consisting predominantly of silver powder mixed with binders and glass frit, used for electronic and solar applications. Based on precedents for silver-filled conductive adhesives and articles of precious metal, it is classified under heading 7115 as an article of precious metal or metal clad with precious metal.

The product is conductive silver paste composed of silver powder dispersed in a polymer and solvent medium with glass frit and organic additives. Heading 3212 covers pigments and metallic powders or flakes dispersed in non-aqueous media in liquid or paste form of a kind used in the manufacture of paints or similar applications. Subheading 321290 is the most specific provision for such pigment preparations in paste form.

The product is a complete, assembled mechanical watch movement with automatic (self-winding) capabilities, fitting squarely into Heading 9108. Specifically, subheading 910820 covers complete and assembled watch movements with automatic winding. Other candidate subheadings include different movement types such as electrically operated or non-automatic ones.

The product is a complete and assembled mechanical watch movement with automatic winding capabilities (TMI NH35). Heading 9108 specifically covers watch movements that are complete and assembled, and subheading 910820 specifically provides for those with automatic winding.

The product is a women's sleeveless knitted poncho, which functions as an outer garment similar to a cape or cloak. Under Chapter 61 Note 4, capes and similar articles are classified in heading 6102, and since the garment is predominantly made of man-made polyester knit fabric, it falls under subheading 610230.

The product is a women's knitted pullover poncho made predominantly of man-made polyester fibers (94%). Under Chapter 61, knit pullovers and similar articles of man-made fibers are classified in heading 6110, specifically subheading 611030.

The products are stainless steel metal storage cabinets designed to be installed in outdoor kitchens and alongside grills for storing objects. They are classified as metal furniture under heading 9403, and specifically as metal furniture other than for office use under subheading 940320.

The items are stainless steel storage cabinets and doors used as built-in components for outdoor kitchens and alongside grills. Based on their structural nature and function as furniture mountings and fittings of base metal rather than standalone furniture, they are classified under heading 8302. Specifically, subheading 830242 covers base metal mountings, fittings, and similar articles suitable for furniture.

The product consists of steel latch actuation rods designed solely for use in vehicle doors to connect the exterior handle to the internal latch. As parts of motor vehicle bodies of headings 8701 through 8705, they are classified under heading 8708 and specifically subheading 870829 for other parts and accessories of motor vehicle bodies.

The products are steel latch actuation rods specially designed and shaped for use in motor vehicle door systems to connect exterior handles to latches. They are classifiable as base metal mountings, fittings and similar articles suitable for motor vehicles under heading 8302.
