Subheading 830230 specifically provides for mountings, fittings and similar articles for motor vehicles, of base metal.

The Honda Acty Van SDX is equipped with seating for four to five persons, sliding doors with windows, and a folding rear seat without a permanent cargo barrier, establishing that it is principally designed for the transport of persons under heading 8703. Because it features a spark-ignition internal combustion engine with a cylinder capacity of 656 cc (not over 1,000 cc), it falls under subheading 870321.

The product is a Honda Acty Van, a motor vehicle principally designed for the transport of persons with seating for four or five and windows in the rear. It falls under heading 8703 for motor cars and other motor vehicles principally designed for the transport of persons. Because it features a spark-ignition internal combustion piston engine with a cylinder capacity not exceeding 1000 cc (656 cc), it is classified in subheading 870321.

The product consists of auger coils made from steel alloys, rolled into a continuous circular helix without a center shaft, representing components of flat-rolled steel further processed into shapes. Based on precedents for steel coils and similar metal components under Chapter 72, they are classified under heading 7210. Subheading 721070 is chosen as the most fitting category for coated/treated steel coils of this form.

The product consists of steel auger coils (helicoid flighting) shaped as a continuous helix, lacking a center shaft. Based on their physical characteristics and dimensions, they are classified under articles of iron or steel in Chapter 73. Among available headings, large tubular or hollow cylindrical structural profiles or similar open profiles of this size fall within Heading 7305 or similar steel article provisions.

The merchandise consists of prepared sweetener blends made from erythritol, monk fruit, allulose, and other components. Food preparations not elsewhere specified or included are classified under heading 2106, specifically subheading 210690.

The products are sweetener blends consisting primarily of polyols and sugars like erythritol and allulose. They are classified under heading 1702, which covers sugars and sugar syrups in solid form not elsewhere specified, specifically falling into the residual subheading 170290 for other sugar blends.

The product consists of semi-finished aluminum plates that are assembled to create a hermetic heatsink for circulating coolant in an energy storage system battery module. As parts of refrigerating or freezing equipment or heat exchange units of heading 8418, they are classifiable under subheading 841899 as parts of refrigerating or freezing equipment other than furniture.

The product consists of aluminum plates used as heatsink components to circulate high-pressure coolant within a battery energy storage system. As parts of heat exchange/refrigerating equipment, they fall under Heading 8418, specifically as parts of refrigerating or freezing equipment under subheading 841899.

The product is a caliper-integrated electronic parking actuator assembly designed exclusively for use in an automotive electronic parking brake system. As a dedicated part for the brake systems of motor vehicles of headings 8701 through 8705, it is classified under heading 8708 and specifically provided for in subheading 870830 covering brakes and parts thereof.

The product is an electronic parking brake actuator assembly designed exclusively for use in automotive braking systems. Under Chapter 87, parts and accessories of motor vehicles specifically designed for brakes and servo-brakes fall under heading 8708, subheading 870830.

The subject merchandise consists of frozen mochi ice treats featuring a frozen filling encased in mochi dough and coated with chocolate, intended for retail sale as a frozen confectionery. Under heading 2105, the terms cover ice cream and other edible ice, which encompasses frozen dessert treats like mochi ice cream or ice novelties. This aligns directly with prior Customs rulings for similar mochi ice confections.

The product is a frozen mochi ice treat consisting of a frozen filling encased in mochi dough and coated with chocolate, intended for retail sale as a frozen confection. Heading 2105 specifically provides for edible ice and ice cream, covering frozen novelties of this nature. Therefore, subheading 210500 is the correct classification.

The product is a bird-shaped glass tealight candle holder made of smooth, clear glass. Under Chapter 70, glassware of a kind used for indoor decoration or similar purposes is classified under heading 7013, and specifically in subheading 701399 as other glass articles not elsewhere specified.

The product is a glass tealight candle holder shaped like a bird, which falls under Chapter 70 covering glass and glassware. Heading 7013 provides for glassware of a kind used for indoor decoration or similar purposes. Since it is neither lead crystal nor specifically enumerated elsewhere under heading 7013, subheading 701399 is the correct classification for other miscellaneous glassware of glass.

The product is an LCD writing tablet designed for writing and drawing with a stylus, featuring an erase button. Under GRI 1 and the terms of Heading 9610, it is classified as a board with a writing or drawing surface. Although it incorporates electronic components for erasing, its principal function remains that of a writing board.

The product is an LCD writing tablet designed for writing and drawing with a stylus and erasing via a button. It functions as an electronic writing board, which is properly covered under Heading 9610 covering slates and boards with writing or drawing surfaces.

The product is a rigid paperboard keepsake box used as a packing/storage container, covered by heading 4819. Because it is a rigid setup box rather than a folding carton or corrugated box, it falls under subheading 481950 for other packing containers of paper or paperboard.

The product is a rigid paperboard keepsake box designed to hold a blanket and a book, suitable for repetitive use. It is classified under heading 4819, which covers boxes and packing containers of paper or paperboard. Specifically, subheading 481950 covers packing containers and similar articles of paper or paperboard not elsewhere specified or included.

The product is a retractable ballpoint pen featuring a message-rotating mechanism. It is classified under heading 9608, which provides for ballpoint pens, and specifically under subheading 960810 as a ball point pen.

The product is a retractable ballpoint pen with a novelty message-rotating feature. It is classified under heading 9608, which provides for ball-point pens, and specifically under subheading 960810 as a ball-point pen.

The electric actuator assembly is an electro-mechanical machine with an individual function (operating an electronic parking brake system) not specified elsewhere in Chapter 84 or Chapter 85. Under similar customs precedents for multi-component active brake devices and electronic braking modules, heading 8479 and specifically subheading 847989 apply.

The product is an Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) actuator assembly designed exclusively for use in motor vehicle braking systems. Under Section XVII, Chapter 87, parts and accessories of motor vehicles are classified in heading 8708, and specifically brakes and servo-brakes and parts thereof fall under subheading 870830.

Midodrine Hydrochloride in bulk powder form is an aromatic amine-function compound. Under Chapter 29 notes, separate chemically defined organic compounds imported in bulk are classified in Chapter 29 rather than as medicaments in Chapter 30. Therefore, it falls under heading 2921 and specifically subheading 292149 as an aromatic monoamine derivative not more specifically provided for.

Midodrine Hydrochloride is an unmixed organic chemical compound with amine-function, specifically an aromatic monoamine derivative, imported in bulk powder form. It is classified under heading 2921 as an amine-function compound, and more specifically under subheading 292149 as an aromatic monoamine derivative not elsewhere specified.

The product is a fully automated post-etch punch machine specifically designed and used for positioning and punching printed circuit board (PCB) panels during manufacturing. Under Chapter 84, Heading 8486 covers machines and apparatus of a kind used solely or principally for the manufacture of semiconductor devices, electronic integrated circuits, or flat panel displays, including handling and processing equipment for related electronic components. Subheading 848640 specifically provides for machines for lifting, handling, loading or unloading or other manufacturing/assembly operations of heading 8486.

The product is a fully automated post-etch punch machine used for positioning and punching printed circuit board (PCB) panels for semiconductor/electronic device manufacturing. Heading 8486 covers machines and apparatus of a kind used solely or principally for the manufacture of semiconductor devices or electronic integrated circuits. Subheading 848640 specifically provides for other specialized machines and material handling equipment of this heading.

The product is a women's knitted pullover made of a blend containing 54 percent cotton, placing it in heading 6110 under knitted pullovers and similar articles. By application of GRI 3(b), cotton provides the essential character of the garment due to its highest percentage content by weight (54%), leading to subheading 611020.

The product is a women's pullover knitted garment made of a blend containing cotton, viscose, polyester, and metallic yarn, with man-made fibers (viscose and polyester) predominating by weight according to general textile classification rules. It is specifically covered by heading 6110, which provides for knitted jerseys, pullovers, and cardigans. Subheading 611030 is chosen because the essential character and predominant fiber content by weight among the textile materials are man-made fibers.

The product is a wireless volume controller that incorporates internal digital-to-analog conversion, audio inputs/outputs, and sound control capabilities for audio systems. Heading 8518 covers audio-frequency electric amplifiers and similar sound control apparatus, making subheading 851840 the most appropriate classification for audio-frequency electric amplifiers and volume control units.

The wireless volume controllers incorporate an internal digital-to-analog converter, wireless communication capabilities, and a digital control interface for audio data transmission and conversion. Heading 8517 covers apparatus for the transmission or reception of voice, images, or other data, specifically including machines for the reception, conversion, and transmission or regeneration of data under subheading 851762.

The Castroviejo caliper is a precision-engineered surgical instrument specially designed for measuring small distances in ophthalmic, dental, and orthopedic procedures. While calipers generally fall under heading 9017, instruments specially designed for use in surgical or medical procedures are classified under heading 9018. Specifically, as a general medical and surgical instrument not provided for more specifically in other subheadings of 9018, it falls under subheading 901890.

The Castroviejo caliper is a precision-engineered surgical instrument primarily used in ophthalmic surgery to measure small distances between anatomical structures. Under Heading 9018, instruments and appliances used in medical or surgical sciences are classified, with subheading 901850 specifically providing for ophthalmic instruments and appliances.

The product consists of auxiliary motorcycle footpeg kits designed specifically for installation on motorcycles. According to Note 2 to Section XVII and heading terms, parts and accessories of motorcycles of heading 8711 are classified under heading 8714. Therefore, subheading 871410 is the correct classification for these motorcycle parts and accessories.

The product consists of auxiliary motorcycle footpeg kits designed solely for use with motorcycles of heading 8711. Under heading 8714, parts and accessories of motorcycles are specifically provided for in subheading 871410.

The product is an imitation meat food preparation made primarily from mycoprotein paste and various seasonings, which is classified in heading 2106 as a food preparation not elsewhere specified or included. Based on prior US Customs precedents for this exact type of imitation meat merchandise, subheading 210690 applies.

The product is an imitation meat food preparation made primarily from mycoprotein paste along with various flavorings and egg white powder. As a food preparation not elsewhere specified or included, it is properly classified under heading 1901 and specifically subheading 190190.

The product is an unpackaged solid bath bar composed of surfactants and other ingredients designed to create bubbles under running water, functioning as a soap or organic surface-active product in the form of a bar for toilet use. Heading 3401 specifically covers organic surface-active products in the form of bars for toilet use, making subheading 340111 the most appropriate classification.

The product is a solid bath bar composed of surface-active agents and other ingredients used under running water to create a fragrant, bubbly bath. Heading 3307 covers bath preparations, and subheading 330730 specifically includes perfumed bath salts and other bath preparations.

The product is an automotive overhead console assembly, which serves as a part or accessory of the motor vehicle body. It is properly classified under heading 8708, specifically subheading 870829, which covers parts and accessories of motor vehicle bodies other than safety seat belts.

The product is an automotive overhead console assembly designed for motor vehicles. Under Section XVII, Chapter 87, parts and accessories of motor vehicle bodies are classified under heading 8708. Specifically, general interior body parts and components not more specifically provided for fall under subheading 870829.

The product consists of cleaned garden cress seeds intended for human consumption as a food ingredient, which are not roasted, cooked, or otherwise prepared. Under heading 1212, vegetable products used primarily for human consumption not elsewhere specified or included are classified. Subheading 121299 specifically covers other vegetable products fit for human consumption, matching precedent rulings for similar edible seeds and plant-based foods.

The product consists of garden cress seeds (Lepidium sativum) intended for human consumption rather than for sowing or pharmaceutical use. They fall under Chapter 12 as oil seeds and oleaginous fruits, specifically as miscellaneous oil seeds in heading 1207 and subheading 120799.

The product is Potassium Chloride Extended-Release Tablets in dosage form, used as an electrolyte replenisher for therapeutic and prophylactic uses. Under GRI 1, it is classified in heading 3004 as a medicament put up in measured doses for retail sale, specifically under subheading 300490 as it does not contain antibiotics, hormones, or alkaloids.

The product is Potassium Chloride in extended-release tablet form, intended for therapeutic or prophylactic use as an electrolyte replenisher. Under Chapter 30, medicaments put up in measured doses for therapeutic use are classified in heading 3004, specifically subheading 300490 as other medicaments not elsewhere specified.

The products are aluminum pill cases designed for personal and home use to hold vitamins and pills. They fall under Heading 7615 as household articles made of aluminum. Subheading 761510 specifically covers table, kitchen, or other household articles and parts thereof of aluminium.

The product is an aluminum case designed to hold pills and vitamins with a lid held by a spring-ball plunger and magnets. Among the available candidate categories, aluminum packaging accessories and closures of base metal fall under heading 8309, specifically subheading 830990 for stoppers, caps, and lids of base metal, or alternatively heading 7616 for other articles of aluminum if treated purely as a miscellaneous aluminum container. Since no exact container heading for non-pocket cases of base metal exists outside chapter 42 (which covers cases with specific outer surfaces like leather or plastic), heading 8309 represents the closest base metal article grouping for metal lids/closures.

The product is a decorative plastic fountain used as an ornamental article for the home or garden. Under heading 3926, plastic statuettes and other ornamental articles are classified in subheading 392640, consistent with previous customs rulings for decorative plastic water globes and similar items.

The product is a decorative plastic fountain used as an ornamental article. It is primarily constructed of plastic and falls under Chapter 39 as an article of plastic, specifically as an ornamental statuette or article under heading 3926.

The product is a portable insulated cooler tote with an exterior of hard-sided molded plastic, making it a similar container to a trunk, case, or box of heading 4202. Specifically, because it has an outer surface of plastics, it is correctly classified under subheading 420212.

The product is a portable insulated cooler tote featuring an exterior of hard-sided molded plastic and a shoulder strap. It is classified under heading 4202 as a similar container/travel bag, specifically under subheading 420292 due to its outer surface of plastic sheeting or molded plastic.

The handheld hair mesotherapy device is an electrically powered personal care appliance designed with a self-contained motor to drive reciprocating needles for skin surface treatment. As a hair-removing or hair-treating/stimulating appliance with a self-contained electric motor, it is properly classified under heading 8510, specifically under subheading 851030 for hair-removing appliances.

The handheld hair mesotherapy device is an electrically powered cosmetic tool containing an internal electric motor that drives reciprocating needles. Because it is an electrical machine with an individual function not specified or included elsewhere in Chapter 85, it is properly classified under heading 8543 and subheading 854370.

The product is a high-pressure hydrogen tank (a composite overwrapped pressure vessel with an internal aluminum liner) designed to store compressed gas. According to GRI 3(b), the essential character of this Type III composite vessel is imparted by the internal aluminum liner, which holds the pressure and contains the gas, leading to classification under heading 7613 as an aluminum container for compressed or liquefied gas.

The product is a high-pressure hydrogen tank (composite overwrapped pressure vessel) designed to store compressed gas. Heading 7311 specifically provides for containers for compressed or liquefied gas of iron or steel, where the essential character of the metal container structure or the applicable provisions for gas containers apply. Therefore, subheading 731100 is the correct classification.

The product consists of replacement needle cartridges, typically used with medical or surgical syringes and appliances. Heading 9018 covers medical, surgical, or veterinary instruments and appliances, and subheading 901831 specifically provides for syringes with or without needles and their related components.

Replacement needle cartridges used for medical or cosmetic tattooing/microneedling procedures are classified under Heading 9018 as instruments and appliances used in medical or surgical sciences. Specifically, subheading 901832 covers tubular metal needles and needles for surgical or medical instruments.

The product is an outdoor mounting kit functioning as a pedestal base/support anchor specifically designed for a Little Free Library. Under Chapter 94, parts of furniture of wood are classified in heading 9403, specifically subheading 940391 for wooden furniture parts. This is more specific than general wood or hardware classifications because the components constitute a dedicated support base and post for the library unit.

The product is an outdoor mounting kit consisting of wood and metal components designed to serve as a pedestal base or support for a Little Free Library. Because it acts as a part of furniture (the library structure), and its essential character is imparted by the wooden post and mounting plate, it is classified under heading 9403 as parts of wooden furniture.

The product is a waterproof boot with an upper primarily of rubber/plastic and an outer sole covered with leather flocking, making the outer sole material considered other than rubber/plastics. Because the outer sole is not rubber/plastic and the upper is not leather or textile, it cannot be classified under headings 6401, 6402, 6403, or 6404, leading to heading 6405 as other footwear. Subheading 640590 applies to footwear n.e.c. in Chapter 64.

The product is a man's above-the-ankle waterproof boot with a rubber/plastic upper and an outer sole having a thick application of leather flocking covering most of the ground-contact surface. Under Note 4(a) to Chapter 64, constituent material of the outer sole is determined by the sole's exterior surface, which in this case is leather flocking rather than rubber or plastics. Therefore, the footwear is classified in heading 6403 with outer soles of leather and uppers of leather or other materials, covering the ankle.

The products are aluminum pill cases designed for personal and home use, falling under household articles of aluminum. Heading 7615 specifically covers aluminum table, kitchen, or other household articles and parts thereof. Therefore, subheading 761510 is the correct and most specific classification.

The product is an aluminum pill case designed to be carried in the pocket or handbag for personal use. Heading 4202 covers articles of a kind normally carried in the pocket or in the handbag, and subheading 420239 provides for such containers made of base materials other than leather, plastic, or textile sheeting (such as aluminum).

The product is a rigid hull inflatable boat for pleasure or sports with a net weight of 226 kg. It falls under Heading 8903 for yachts and other vessels for pleasure or sports, specifically under inflatable vessels exceeding 100 kg in unladen net weight.

The product is a rigid hull inflatable boat designed for pleasure or sports, classified under heading 8903. Because it is inflatable and has an unladen net weight of 226 kg (exceeding 100 kg), it specifically falls under subheading 890319.

The product is a citronella candle consisting of paraffin wax and a single wick housed in a glass jar. Candles and similar articles are specifically provided for under heading 3406 by application of GRI 1. The presence of a glass holder does not change its classification as a candle.

The product is a citronella candle consisting of paraffin wax and citronella oil in a glass holder, which is specifically provided for under Heading 3406 as candles, tapers and the like. Therefore, it is correctly classified in subheading 340600.

The product consists of aluminum pill cases designed for personal and home use, which are classified as other household articles of aluminium under heading 7615. Subheading 761510 covers aluminium table, kitchen, or other household articles and parts thereof. This matches precedents for household aluminum articles and aligns with heading 7615's scope for non-travel household utility articles.

The product is an aluminum pill case with multiple compartments and a spring-ball plunger lid, designed for personal or home use. Because it is an article made of aluminum that does not fall under more specific headings in Chapter 76 or other chapters, it is classified under other articles of aluminum in heading 7616. Specifically, subheading 761699 covers other articles of aluminum not elsewhere specified.

The products are organic surface-active preparations and soap used for skin washing, presented in moulded shapes and impregnated paper for toilet use. Heading 3401 specifically covers soap and organic surface-active products in the form of bars, cakes, moulded shapes, and paper for toilet use. Subheading 340111 provides the most specific classification for these items.

The products are skin-washing preparations presented in molded shapes or forms for toilet use, falling under heading 3401. Specifically, the solid molded shower gel and related items are classified under subheading 340111 as organic surface-active products in the form of bars, cakes, or moulded shapes for toilet use.

The product is a fluid strainer designed to remove particulate matter and debris from process media using an internal screen to protect downstream components. It is classified under heading 8421, which covers filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for liquids, specifically under subheading 842129 for other filtering machinery for liquids not elsewhere specified.

The LPD strainers are mechanical devices used to filter and remove particulate matter and debris from process liquids to protect downstream components. Filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for liquids are specifically provided for under heading 8421, specifically subheading 842129 for general liquid filtering or purifying machinery.

The product is a complete soldier costume consisting of multiple pieces designed for festive or entertainment wear, such as costuming or role-playing. Under Note 1(t) to Chapter 61/62, apparel of a kind used for masquerades or similar entertainment is excluded from chapters 61 and 62 and classified in heading 9505. Therefore, it falls under subheading 950590.

The product is a British Redcoat soldier costume comprised of multiple pieces including a coat, vest, and pants made from knitted polyester fabric, classified as a men's ensemble under heading 6103. Subheading 610323 specifically covers men's or boys' ensembles of synthetic fibres, which are knitted or crocheted. The components function together as an ensemble for costuming purposes.

The product is a steel frame weldment component (base frame) designed as a structural platform for a manufacturing cell. According to Note 1 to Chapter 73 and the terms of heading 7308, steel structures and parts thereof are classified under heading 7308. Since these weldments are imported separately without the machinery and serve as general structural framework, they are classified under subheading 730890 as other structures and parts of iron or steel.

The product is a steel weldment frame base specifically engineered for a containerized robotic industrial forming and metal-working cell. As a part solely or principally used with metal-forming machine tools of Heading 8462, it classifies under the provisions for those machine-tools and their parts. Among the candidate subheadings under Heading 8462, code 846229 covers other numerically controlled bending, folding, straightening, or flattening machine parts or related metal-working machine tools.

ZIEXTENZO is a leukocyte growth factor biosimilar, which falls under immunological products obtained by biotechnological processes and put up in measured doses in prefilled syringes for retail sale. Therefore, heading 3002 and specifically subheading 300215 properly cover this biotechnological therapeutic product.

ZIEXTENZO is a leukocyte growth factor biosimilar imported in prefilled syringes in measured doses for therapeutic use. Under Heading 3004, it is classified as a medicament consisting of mixed or unmixed products for therapeutic use, put up in measured doses or packed for retail sale. Therefore, subheading 300490 is the correct and most specific classification.

The product consists of aluminum pill cases intended for personal and home use, which are properly classified under heading 7615 as aluminum household articles. Based on precedents for similar aluminum containers and household articles, subheading 761510 is the most specific and correct classification.

The product consists of aluminum cases designed for personal use to hold pills and vitamins, which are of a kind normally carried in the pocket or handbag. Heading 4202 covers articles of a kind normally carried in the pocket or in the handbag. Since the outer surface and material is base metal (aluminum) rather than leather, plastics, or textile sheeting, it falls under the 'other' subheading of 420239.

The product is a park rod designed to function as a linkage between electrical actuation and the park gear of a motor vehicle. As a dedicated part of a motor vehicle transmission or shifting mechanism not more specifically provided for elsewhere, it is classified under heading 8708 as a motor vehicle part. Specifically, subheading 870899 covers other parts and accessories of motor vehicles not elsewhere specified or included.

The product is a park rod made from cold-drawn round steel wire that has been bent into a specific configuration, classified as a cold-formed iron or non-alloy steel bar or rod under Chapter 72. Heading 7215 covers other bars and rods of iron or non-alloy steel not elsewhere specified, and subheading 721550 specifically provides for cold-formed or cold-finished bars and rods.

The product is a linear acting hydraulic cylinder designed to convert fluid pressure into linear force to control aircraft ailerons. Heading 8412 covers hydraulic power engines and motors, and subheading 841221 specifically provides for linear acting hydraulic cylinders.

The product is a linear acting hydraulic cylinder used to convert fluid pressure into linear force. Under Heading 8412, hydraulic power engines and motors that are linear acting (cylinders) are specifically provided for in subheading 841221.

The products are weekly AM-PM pill and vitamin cases made entirely from aluminum alloy. Heading 7615 covers household articles of aluminum, which includes aluminum containers and household organizers of this nature.

The product consists of aluminum pill cases made of aluminum alloy, designed to hold pills or vitamins. Since they are not classified under more specific headings for travel goods or plastics, they fall under general articles of aluminum in Chapter 76. Therefore, subheading 761699 covers other articles of aluminum not elsewhere specified.

The product is a Type III composite overwrapped pressure vessel consisting of an internal aluminum liner with a composite carbon fiber and epoxy overwrap, designed for storing high-pressure gas. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of the composite cylinder is imparted by its internal aluminum liner which contains the pressurized gas, classifying it under heading 7613 as an aluminum container for compressed or liquefied gas.

The product is a Type III composite overwrapped pressure vessel consisting of an internal aluminum liner with carbon fiber/epoxy overwrap, designed for storing high-pressure gas. By application of GRI 3(b), the essential character of the composite cylinder is imparted by its internal metal (aluminum) liner which holds the gas and provides the primary structural vessel capability. Therefore, it is classified under heading 7613 as an aluminum container for compressed or liquefied gas.

The product is a hobbyist craft kit designed for hand-forming and polishing decorative clay spheres, featuring kaolin and red French clays as its functional core. Under heading 3407, modeling pastes and similar preparations put up in sets for retail sale are classified here, supported by precedent rulings on craft pottery kits and air-dry clay kits.

The product is a craft kit containing unworked clays (kaolin and red French clay) as its functional core, which give the good its essential character under GRI 3(b). Heading 2508 covers other clays not elsewhere specified or included. Subheading 250840 provides the appropriate 6-digit classification for these miscellaneous natural clays.

The product is a made-up polishing or buffing cloth made of 100 percent cotton woven fabric with sewn edges, measuring 17 x 11 inches. Heading 6307 covers made-up textile articles not elsewhere specified, and subheading 630710 specifically provides for floor cloths, dish-cloths, dusters and similar cleaning cloths.

The product is a made up textile article, specifically a polishing or buffing cloth made of woven cotton fabric with sewn edges. Under Heading 6307, made-up cleaning cloths, dusters, and similar polishing or buffing cloths are specifically provided for in subheading 630710.

The product consists of cooked, smoked, and seasoned quail eggs in a vacuum-sealed pouch, containing added sugar, starch syrup, and other ingredients making it a prepared food product. Heading 2106 covers food preparations not elsewhere specified or included, and pre-seasoned, ready-to-eat items of this nature fall into subheading 210690.

The product consists of smoked quail eggs not in their shell, which have been cooked and seasoned. Heading 0408 covers birds' eggs not in shell, and subheading 040899 specifically includes birds' eggs that are fresh, cooked by steaming or boiling in water, moulded, frozen, or otherwise preserved, including with added sugar or other sweetening matter.

The product is an empty, unequipped steel storage cabinet designed to secure computer servers and networking equipment. It is described by the terms of heading 9403 as other metal furniture. Subheading 940320 specifically provides for metal furniture other than for office use, aligning with the established classification precedents for such server racks.

The product is a floor-standing, empty, and unequipped steel storage cabinet designed to secure computer server equipment and networking devices. Under Chapter 94, heading 9403 covers other furniture and parts thereof, and specifically 940320 covers metal furniture. Therefore, it is properly classified as other metal furniture.

The product is an empty, floor-standing metal storage cabinet (rack) designed to secure computer server and networking equipment. Under Chapter 94, heading 9403 covers other metal furniture, which includes server racks and computer cabinets not specifically intended for office use or electrical control distribution.

The product is an empty, unequipped steel storage cabinet designed to house electrical control, distribution, and server equipment such as power distribution units and switches. Unequipped cabinets and similar bases intended for goods of heading 8537 are specifically provided for under subheading 853810 as parts suitable for use solely or principally with electric control and distribution apparatus.

The product is a floor-standing, empty, and unequipped modular steel storage cabinet system designed to house various components. It falls under Heading 9403 as metal furniture, specifically under subheading 940320 for metal furniture other than for office use, as supported by consistent customs precedents.

The product is a floor-standing, empty steel storage cabinet designed for modular configuration and storage. Under Chapter 94, heading 9403 covers other furniture and parts thereof, and metal furniture not specified for office use falls specifically under subheading 940320.

The product is a men's faux leather jacket with an outer shell of cellular polyurethane plastic on a polyester woven backing. Under Note 2 to Chapter 39, garments made of cellular plastic combined with a textile backing are classified in Chapter 62 (heading 6210) as garments made up of the fabrics of heading 5903. Therefore, it falls under subheading 621020 for men's or boys' overcoats, anoraks, and similar articles of heading 5903.

The product is a men's jacket with an outer shell composed of cellular polyurethane plastic material supported by a polyester woven fabric backing for reinforcement. According to Note 2 to Chapter 59, textile fabrics combined with polyurethane are classified in heading 5903, and garments made up of these fabrics fall under heading 6210. Specifically, men's jackets and similar articles of such fabrics are provided for in subheading 621020.

The product is a foldable cushioned play mat made of polyurethane foam covered with fabric, designed for children to play, lounge, or nap. Based on precedent for combination toddler mattress/playmats, it is classified under heading 9404 as an article of bedding or similar furnishing. Subheading 940490 specifically covers bedding and similar furnishing articles not elsewhere specified.

The product is a foldable cushioned play space designed for young children to play, lounge, or nap, constructed with a polyurethane foam core and covered with textile materials. Under GRI 1, it is classified as an article of bedding or similar stuffed furnishing of Chapter 94. Heading 9404 covers cushions, mattresses, and similar stuffed furnishings, making subheading 940490 the most appropriate provision for other articles of bedding and similar furnishings.

The product is a nasal atomizer assembly specifically designed to deliver atomized medication into the nasal passage, functioning as a medical appliance. Under Heading 9018, it is classified as a medical instrument and appliance, specifically within subheading 901839 as a medical appliance comparable to cannulae and other medical delivery instruments.

The provided candidate list does not contain an exact heading for medical instruments or plastic parts of syringes (such as Chapter 90). Among the choices provided, heading 3006 covers pharmaceutical goods and related medical/surgical adjuncts, though none directly describe a standalone plastic nasal atomizer assembly.

The product is an insulated electrical power cable fitted with connectors (plugs) at both ends for voltages not exceeding 1000 volts. Heading 8544 covers insulated electric conductors, and subheading 854442 specifically provides for those fitted with connectors.

The product is an insulated electrical power cable fitted with connectors for a voltage not exceeding 1000 volts. Heading 8544 specifically covers insulated wire, cable, and other electric conductors fitted with connectors. Subheading 854442 applies directly to insulated electric conductors for a voltage not exceeding 1000 volts that are fitted with connectors.

The product consists of apparel designed specifically for toy minifigures, making it an accessory to a toy rather than human apparel of Chapters 61 or 62. Under Chapter 95, items designed for amusement, entertainment, or doll-like accessories are classified as festive, carnival, or other entertainment articles under heading 9505. Therefore, subheading 950590 is the appropriate classification.

The product consists of apparel items designed for toys (minifigures). Although apparel for dolls or toys is typically classified under Chapter 95, no Chapter 95 candidate subheadings were provided. Among the available Chapter 62 options, trousers and shorts of synthetic fibers under heading 6203 represent the closest structural fit for synthetic textile pieces like the loincloth.

The product is a full-bodied plush teddy bear designed for hugging or display, which falls under the terms of Heading 9503 as a toy representing animals. Despite its promotional and awareness-raising purpose, stuffed animals of this type are classified as toys under subheading 950300, consistent with similar US Customs precedents for plush character items.
The product is a plush teddy bear designed as a toy or collectible. None of the provided candidate subheadings correspond to toys of Chapter 95, but the item is fundamentally a plush toy bear.

The product is an empty, floor-standing steel storage cabinet designed for IT or network equipment (a rack/enclosure). It is classified under heading 9403 as other metal furniture, aligning with multiple Customs precedents for metal storage cabinets. Subheading 940320 specifically covers metal furniture other than for office use, as server and network racks are generally categorized outside traditional office furniture.

The product is a floor-standing steel storage cabinet (rack) designed to house computer and networking equipment, which falls under Chapter 94 as other metal furniture. Heading 9403 specifically covers other furniture and parts thereof, and subheading 940320 covers other metal furniture. The other candidate chapters cover base metal products, iron and steel, or machinery, but floor-standing storage racks are classified as general metal furniture.

The product is a composite knee protector designed for roofers, constructed of rubber, EVA foam, and polyurethane foam covered with fabric. Under GRI 3(b), the rubber outer layer provides the essential character, but knee pads are generally classified as made up textile articles of heading 6307 per established precedents. Therefore, subheading 630790 applies to these made-up textile and composite knee pads.

The product is an ergonomic knee protector (kneepad) constructed predominantly of vulcanized rubber, which imparts its essential character under GRI 3(b). Heading 4015 specifically covers articles of apparel and clothing accessories of vulcanized rubber other than hard rubber, making subheading 401590 the correct classification for other clothing accessories such as kneepads.

The product is a cutting board system primarily made of acacia wood, which is a tropical wood, accompanied by removable steel components. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of the composite good is imparted by the wooden cutting board. Therefore, it is classified under heading 4419 as tableware and kitchenware of wood, specifically of tropical wood.

The product is a two-sided cutting board made of acacia wood (a tropical wood) with supplementary metal accessories. Under Heading 4419, which covers tableware and kitchenware of wood, items made of tropical wood are specifically classified under subheading 441920.

The product is a CNC horizontal turning-milling machine combining turning and secondary machining operations like milling and drilling. Machines for treating metal with individual functions not more specifically provided for elsewhere are covered under heading 8479. Subheading 847981 specifically provides for machines and mechanical appliances for treating metal.

The product is a CNC horizontal turning-milling machine featuring a tool turret with live tooling capability for milling, drilling, and secondary operations, classified under heading 8459 for machine-tools for milling by removing metal. Subheading 845961 covers numerically controlled milling machines, which accurately describes its primary capability.

The Deray SpliceMan 2.0 is an electro-thermic appliance using infrared quartz emitters to shrink sleeves on wire splice joints. It is classified under heading 8516 as an electro-thermic appliance not elsewhere specified or included.

The infrared heat shrink machine is designed to treat materials (sleeves on wire splices) by a process involving a change of temperature using heating elements. Heading 8419 covers machinery for the treatment of materials by a process involving a change of temperature, and subheading 841989 specifically provides for other non-domestic machinery, plant, and laboratory equipment for this purpose.

The product is a handmade decorative wall sign made of steel wire entirely encased in a cotton tubular braid, functioning as a textile furnishing article for interior decoration. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of this wall hanging is imparted by the exterior cotton tubular braid rather than the internal metal wire used solely for structural support. Therefore, it is classified under heading 6304 as other furnishing articles, specifically of cotton under subheading 630492.

The product is a handmade decorative wall hanging formed into words and shapes using steel wire concealed within a cotton tubular braid, functioning as a sign or symbol. Heading 8310 specifically provides for sign plates, name-plates, and similar plates, numbers, letters and other symbols, of base metal. Because the steel wire provides the structural shape while the article functions as a lettered or symbolic sign, 831000 is the correct subheading.

The products are zinc-plated carbon steel hydraulic hose crimp fittings used for connecting flexible hydraulic hoses. Heading 7307 provides for tube or pipe fittings of iron or steel. Since they are made of non-stainless carbon steel and do not fall under specific categories like cast or threaded elbows/bends, they are classified in subheading 730799 as other iron or steel tube or pipe fittings.

The product is a zinc-plated carbon steel hydraulic hose fitting designed for connecting hoses in hydraulic circuits. Under heading 7307, tube or pipe fittings of iron or steel (other than stainless steel) that are not specifically enumerated in other subheadings fall under the residual category 730799.

The product is a stainless-steel ring-shank nail used for decking. Heading 7317 specifically covers nails, tacks, and similar articles of iron or steel. Therefore, subheading 731700 is the correct classification for these iron or steel nails.

The product is a stainless-steel nail used for construction and patio/deck work. Heading 7317 specifically provides for nails and similar articles of iron or steel, covering stainless steel nails under subheading 731700.

The product is a craft kit for making paper flowers, consisting primarily of creped paper sheets, wire, and instructions. Under GRI 1 and 3(b), the essential character of the kit is imparted by the paper, making heading 4823 appropriate for articles of paper not elsewhere specified or included.

The product is a craft kit consisting principally of rectangular sheets of creped paper, along with floral wire and templates, intended for making paper flowers. Under GRI 3(b), the essential character of the kit is imparted by the creped paper sheets, which fall under heading 4808 as non-kraft creped paper in sheets. Therefore, subheading 480890 is the correct classification for the creped paper sheets that form the core of the kit.

The product is a tactile audio device that converts ambient sound into physical vibration via a microphone and internal processing circuitry. It functions essentially as an audio processing and reproducing apparatus intended for use with media and entertainment. Based on precedents for baby sound machines and sound reproduction devices, it falls under heading 8519.

The product is a vibrating sound conversion device containing a microphone, internal audio processing circuitry, and a haptic vibration motor that acts as a semiconductor-based transducer to convert ambient sound into physical vibration. It is classified under heading 8541 as a semiconductor-based transducer. Subheading 854151 specifically provides for semiconductor-based transducers.

The products are swivel casters designed specifically as parts for office chairs. Following precedent for furniture parts and heading 9401 terms for seats and their parts, they are classified under subheading 940199 as parts of seats.

The product consists of swivel casters made of steel and other materials. None of the provided candidate subheadings specifically cover furniture casters (which typically fall under heading 8302). Selecting a default placeholder code from the available list since no matching heading for casters is present in the candidate list.

The product is a counter display unit made of corrugated cardboard, functioning essentially as a container or tray used for holding and displaying items in stores. Heading 4819 covers cartons, boxes, and cases of corrugated paper or paperboard. Subheading 481910 specifically provides for boxes and cases of corrugated paper or paperboard.

The product is a counter display unit constructed of corrugated cardboard, which is specifically described by heading 4808 for corrugated paper and paperboard. Subheading 480810 covers corrugated paper and paperboard in rolls or sheets, which is the foundational material used to construct these display units.

The product is a women's clog-style shoe with molded rubber or plastic uppers and outer soles, not covering the ankle. Under Heading 6402, it is classified in subheading 640299 because it does not cover the ankle, is not waterproof, and is not sports footwear.

The product is a women's clog-style shoe with an upper and outer sole made of molded rubber/plastics, classified under Heading 6402 as footwear with outer soles and uppers of rubber or plastics. Because it does not cover the ankle, is not waterproof, and lacks upper straps assembled with plugs, it falls under subheading 640299. The external leather application on the outsole does not change the essential character of the molded rubber/plastic upper and sole.

The product is a softcover medical textbook containing printed pages and instructional information on human anatomy. Heading 4901 covers printed books, brochures, and similar printed matter, and subheading 490199 specifically provides for printed books other than children's picture books or dictionaries.

The product is a softcover textbook for medical students titled 'Gray's Anatomy for Students'. It is classified under Heading 4901, which covers printed books and similar printed matter, specifically under subheading 490199 as other printed books not elsewhere specified.

The product is Tegoprazan in tablet form packaged for therapeutic use, which classifies it as a medicament under heading 3004. As it does not contain antibiotics, hormones, alkaloids, or vitamins, it falls under the residual subheading 300490, matching numerous similar precedents.

Tegoprazan tablets are formulated in measured doses as a pharmaceutical medicament for therapeutic use in treating gastroesophageal reflux disease. Heading 3004 specifically covers medicaments consisting of mixed or unmixed products for therapeutic uses, put up in measured doses or packed for retail sale. Therefore, subheading 300490 is the appropriate classification for these other miscellaneous medicaments.

The product is a semiconductor photolithography wafer stage module designed to position silicon wafers during exposure and metrology within an EUV lithography system. Heading 8486 specifically covers machines and apparatus of a kind used solely or principally for the manufacture of semiconductor devices or electronic integrated circuits, and subheading 848640 applies to specialized handling and positioning modules of this nature.

The product is a semiconductor photolithography wafer stage module, which acts as a specialized positioning unit for semiconductor lithography systems. It is classified under heading 8486 as parts and accessories of machines used solely or principally for the manufacture of semiconductor devices, specifically falling under subheading 848690 as parts.

The product consists of electrical cables constructed of insulated wire and fitted with connectors (terminal rings or female connectors) used as battery or ground jumpers in trucks and trailers. Under heading 8544, insulated electric conductors fitted with connectors for voltages not exceeding 1000 volts are specifically classified in subheading 854442.

The product consists of electrical cables constructed of a single insulated wire fitted with connectors (terminal rings or female electrical connectors) for low voltage use. Heading 8544 specifically covers insulated electric conductors fitted with connectors. Subheading 854442 is the most specific provision for insulated electric conductors not exceeding 1000 volts that are fitted with connectors.

The product is a diesel-hydraulic self-propelled mobile concrete sprayer designed for mining operations. Under GRI 1, mechanical appliances for projecting, dispersing, or spraying liquids or powders are classified under heading 8424. Specifically, subheading 842489 covers mechanical appliances for spraying for non-agricultural use.

The product is a self-propelled mobile concrete sprayer equipped with a concrete pumping mechanism for mining operations. Under heading 8413, concrete pumps are specifically provided for in subheading 841340, which covers pumps specifically designed for concrete handling and spraying applications.

The mobile container carrier is a non-self-propelled multi-unit vehicle system designed to lift and transport ISO shipping containers using wheels, towing bars, and hydraulic lifting frames. Based on precedents for industrial trailers and non-self-propelled transport equipment, it is classified under heading 8716 as a trailer/semi-trailer or non-mechanically propelled vehicle for transport. Subheading 871639 covers other trailers and semi-trailers not specified elsewhere.

The product is a mobile lifting system comprising four corner units designed to lift and transport ISO shipping containers, falling under heading 8426 as mobile lifting frames on tyres. Subheading 842612 specifically covers mobile lifting frames on tyres and straddle carriers, perfectly matching the design and operational capability of the container carrier.

The product is a protective cellphone case made of plastic composite (G10) with varying bezels, which is classified as an article of plastic under heading 3926. Past Customs rulings consistently classify smartphone and electronic device cases of this nature under subheading 392690 as other articles of plastics.

The product is a protective cellphone case designed to hold and protect a smartphone. Under the Harmonized System, similar containers and cases of a kind designed to carry or protect specific personal items such as phones are classified under Heading 4202, specifically subheading 420292 when having an outer surface of plastic or textile materials or composite construction.

The product is a crankshaft position sensor used solely or principally with motor vehicle internal combustion engines. As a specialized part of motor vehicles of Chapter 87, it is classified under heading 8708 and specifically within subheading 870899 as a general motor vehicle part and accessory not more specifically provided for.

The xRover mobility strollers are specifically designed for the transport of persons with disabilities, fitting the description of carriages for disabled persons. As they are non-motorized and caregiver-propelled, they fall under heading 8713, which covers carriages for disabled persons whether or not mechanically propelled. Subheading 8713.10 is the most specific classification for non-mechanically propelled carriages for disabled persons.

The Aqua Doodle Book is primarily a children's coloring book that uses water to reveal images, falling squarely under the terms of heading 4903. Despite the inclusion of a water pen, the essential character of the item is that of a printed children's coloring book, consistent with established precedents for similar educational and recreational printed matter.

The knee protectors are made of a combination of plastic foam and textile straps, which does not fit into the specific categories for footwear or sports equipment. As they are made-up textile and plastic articles not elsewhere specified or included in the Harmonized System, they are classified under heading 6307. This is consistent with established US Customs rulings for general-purpose knee pads.

The Fento Max knee protectors are made of plastic foam and textile straps, designed for industrial or general use rather than specific athletic or medical purposes. As they are not specifically provided for elsewhere in the nomenclature, they are classified as made-up textile articles under heading 6307. This is consistent with established customs precedents for general-purpose knee pads.

The product is a container designed for the storage and transport of trading cards and gaming accessories. Under Heading 4202, it is classified as a container of a kind similar to those listed, and because it is made of plastic, it falls under the subheading for containers with an outer surface of sheeting of plastics.

The product is an aluminum box designed for the storage of keys, which falls under the heading for aluminum containers. As it is a rigid aluminum box with a capacity of less than 300 liters and lacks mechanical or thermal equipment, it is classified under subheading 7612.90.

The product is a set of hand tools for home repairs put up for retail sale. Heading 8206 specifically covers sets consisting of two or more tools of headings 8202 to 8205, which is the appropriate classification for a retail tool kit.

The industrial water cooling tower is a machine designed to treat water by changing its temperature through evaporation, which falls under the scope of heading 8419. As it is not a heat exchange unit (which typically involves closed-circuit heat transfer) and is not for domestic use, it is most appropriately classified under the residual subheading 841989 for machinery for treating materials by a change of temperature.

The product is a floor-standing wooden bookshelf, which is classified as furniture under heading 9403. As it is made of wood and is not specifically for office, kitchen, or bedroom use, it falls under the residual category for other wooden furniture in subheading 940360.

The Fento Display-Stand is a floor-standing metal structure designed for retail display, which falls under the category of furniture. According to Chapter 94, Note 2, the term 'furniture' includes articles designed for placing on the floor and used for display purposes, and since it is made of metal and not for office use, it is classified under 940320.

The product is a women's knit blouse made primarily of man-made fibers (modal, polyester, nylon, and spandex). Under GRI 1 and the chapter notes for Chapter 61, it is classified in heading 6106 as a knitted blouse, and specifically in subheading 610620 because the man-made fiber content exceeds that of any other single textile material.

The product is a ceramic household article made of dolomite, which is not porcelain or china. Heading 6912 covers ceramic household articles other than porcelain or china, and precedents confirm that ceramic household items are classified here rather than as ornamental statuettes under 6913.

The product is aluminum foil with a thickness not exceeding 0.2mm, which falls under heading 7607. As it is not backed with any other material, it is classified under subheading 760711, which specifically covers rolled aluminum foil that has not been further worked.

The industrial water cooling tower is a machine designed to treat water by changing its temperature through evaporation, which falls under the scope of heading 8419. As it is not a domestic appliance, a heat exchange unit, or a specific type of dryer or heater listed in other subheadings, it is most appropriately classified under the residual category for machinery for treating materials by a change of temperature.
